```ts
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { MediaDeps } from "./context";
import { finalize } from "./flows/status";
import { requestOwed } from "./owed";

/** An upload the worker has not answered for this long has failed. Normal processing takes seconds. */
export const PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60_000;
/** An upload nobody put on a post within a day is removed. */
export const UNATTACHED_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;
/** Files without a row are only treated as orphans once they are this old, so work in flight is never touched. */
export const ORPHAN_AGE_MS = 60 * 60_000;
/**
 * A deletion request stays at least this long. The worker may be in the middle of an image when
 * the request arrives, and writes its files afterwards; one image takes at most two minutes before
 * the worker's watchdog ends it, so after ten the request has been seen with everything in place.
 */
export const DELETION_GRACE_MS = 10 * 60_000;
export const SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;
export const RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 60_000;
/**
 * Reconcile refuses to delete images without a row when there are more of them than both of these:
 * a database restored from an older snapshot has rows missing for every image posted since, and
 * those images must not go. MEDIA_RECONCILE=force overrides it once the operator has checked.
 */
export const RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS = 50;
export const RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE = 0.02;

export interface SweepReport {
  finalized: number;
  timedOut: number;
  expired: number;
  withdrawn: number;
  orphans: number;
  /** Orphan images the reconcile pass refused to delete. */
  refused: number;
}

/**
 * Housekeeping that no request triggers. It is a plain function of the clock, so tests call it
 * with whatever time they need. Every step is safe to repeat and safe to run next to live traffic.
 */
export async function sweep(deps: MediaDeps, now: Date, options: { reconcile: boolean }): Promise<SweepReport> {
  const report: SweepReport = { finalized: 0, timedOut: 0, expired: 0, withdrawn: 0, orphans: 0, refused: 0 };

  // 1. Results nobody asked for: the composer was closed, or the post was written from another device.
  for (const id of await deps.repo.processingIds()) {
    if (await finalize(deps, id)) report.finalized++;
  }

  // 2. Uploads the worker never answered, because it was down or the file killed it three times. 3b Task 5: never an
  //    imported image of an import whose row exists, which the import settles itself after IMPORT_RULES.checkHours (its
  //    feeder puts at most two in the worker's way, and a busy worker is no failure of the image).
  const stale = await deps.repo.failStale(new Date(now.getTime() - PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS));
  // 3. Uploads nobody posted. 3b Task 5: never an imported image of an import whose row exists, which waits for its post
  //    however long the preparation takes, or goes with the import's leftovers (import-drive, media.forImports).
  const expired = await deps.repo.deleteUnattachedBefore(new Date(now.getTime() - UNATTACHED_TTL_MS));
  report.timedOut = stale.length;
  report.expired = expired.length;
  for (const id of [...stale, ...expired]) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
  await deps.files.requestDeletion([...stale, ...expired]);

  // 4. Deletions that are owed: rows the account's purge or the disposal deleted whose request was never written (the
  //    process stopped after the commit, or the request failed), asked for now; and the notes of rows that are still
  //    there, forgotten once they are stale. Every pass, so a request that could not be written is retried within
  //    thirty seconds of the volume taking writes again, however many files it names: these are known deletions, not
  //    orphans, and the reconcile pass below never has to judge them.
  await requestOwed(deps, now.getTime());

  // 5. Deletion requests the worker has carried out, once they are old enough to have covered late writes.
  for (const { id, ageMs } of await deps.files.deletionRequestAges(now.getTime())) {
    if (ageMs < DELETION_GRACE_MS || (await deps.files.imageRemains(id))) continue;
    await deps.files.withdrawDeletion(id);
    report.withdrawn++;
  }

  // 6. What a crash between a commit and a file operation left behind, and the files of deleted
  //    accounts, whose rows went by cascade.
  if (options.reconcile && deps.reconcileMode !== "off") {
    const nowMs = now.getTime();
    const stored = await deps.files.storedImages(nowMs);
    const images = stored.filter((entry) => entry.ageMs > ORPHAN_AGE_MS).map((entry) => entry.id);
    const uploads = (await deps.files.storedUploads(nowMs)).filter((entry) => entry.ageMs > ORPHAN_AGE_MS).map((entry) => entry.id);
    const known = await deps.repo.existing([...new Set([...images, ...uploads])]);
    const orphanImages = images.filter((id) => !known.has(id));
    const orphanUploads = uploads.filter((id) => !known.has(id));
    for (const id of orphanUploads) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
    const tooMany = orphanImages.length > RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS && orphanImages.length > stored.length * RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE;
    if (tooMany && deps.reconcileMode !== "force") {
      report.refused = orphanImages.length;
      report.orphans = orphanUploads.length;
      deps.log.error(
        { images: orphanImages.length, stored: stored.length },
        "media: reconcile refused to delete this many images without a row. If the database was restored from an older snapshot, restore the store from the same one; if the images are really orphans, set MEDIA_RECONCILE=force for one pass",
      );
    } else {
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(orphanImages);
      report.orphans = orphanImages.length + orphanUploads.length;
      if (report.orphans > 0) deps.log.warn({ images: orphanImages.length, uploads: orphanUploads.length }, "media: removed files that had no row");
    }
  }
  return report;
}

/**
 * The sweeper as a job: one instance at a time, rounds never overlapping, the lock refreshed while a
 * long reconcile runs. The reconcile marker is a second key that simply expires every ten minutes.
 */
export function createSweeper(deps: MediaDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  let last: SweepReport | null = null;
  const job = createJob({
    name: "media-sweeper",
    intervalMs: SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS,
    lockTtlMs: SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS,
    lock,
    log: deps.log,
    run: async () => {
      const reconcile = await lock.acquire("job:media-sweeper:reconcile", "due", RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS);
      last = await sweep(deps, deps.now(), { reconcile });
    },
  });
  return {
    /** One round now: the report, or null when another instance holds the lock or a round is still in flight. */
    async round(): Promise<SweepReport | null> {
      last = null;
      return (await job.round()) === "ran" ? last : null;
    },
    /** Sweeps every thirty seconds until the returned function is called. */
    start: job.start,
  };
}
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ALERT_RULES, PUSH_KINDS, type AlertChannelState, type AlertFacts, type AlertKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { StaffAlertKind, StaffMessage } from "../auth";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { urgentWaiting } from "./repo";

/**
 * Staff alerts (3c design, section 7.12; 3f design, sections 5 and 7.2). Every alert has two legs. The push: one row of
 * alert_outbox, which the watcher (apps/api/src/notify) publishes to the phones with the fixed sentence of its kind,
 * counts and times only. The mail: to every live staff account, with counts and times and, for 3c's and 3e's kinds, the
 * staff handle where they name one; never a link or content. The moderation module, which never sees an address, keeps
 * each alert's throttle as one key of the shared limit store, and the alert tick below writes the time-driven alerts
 * (alert_steps()) and mails every 3f alert whose mail is its push's sentence, whoever wrote its row.
 */

/** The key and the window of the urgent lane's alert. The dispatch job repeats the alert under the same key. */
export const URGENT_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-urgent";
export const URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60_000;

/** The alert tick's name: its lock is `job:alert-tick`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const ALERT_TICK_JOB = "alert-tick";
/** The time between the end of one round of the tick and the start of the next. */
export const ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS = ALERT_RULES.tickSeconds * 1000;
/**
 * The alert tick's mail leg, a job of its own (3f's review, operations2): its lock is `job:alert-mail`, and a round comes
 * ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended. A relay that answers slowly or not at all then holds only the mail
 * leg: alert_steps() and the channel's check keep their own time, so the pushes they write (the 15-minute escalation,
 * the deadline's reminders) are never late behind a mail.
 */
export const ALERT_MAIL_JOB = "alert-mail";

/**
 * The kinds whose mail is their push's sentence that the tick mails from a row, each a template of the mailer: every
 * kind of the contracts' SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS, which a test holds this list to (3f's review, operations4: Task 5's two
 * kinds were pushed and never mailed).
 */
export const TICK_MAILED_KINDS: readonly StaffAlertKind[] = [
  "contact_mail",
  "contact_mail_escalated",
  "order_due",
  "mailbox_unreachable",
  "alert_channel_down",
  "order_opened",
  "order_corrected",
  "order_unverified",
  // Task 3.
  "order_effected",
  "order_reinstated",
  "hold_ending",
  // Task 6: copy_overdue, which alert_steps() writes daily, and copy_taken, which staffAlert writes after a download.
  "copy_overdue",
  "copy_taken",
  // Task 5's two daily kinds, joined in 3f's review: a report to an authority owed, and a hand-over's copy not destroyed.
  "report_owed",
  "handover_undestroyed",
  // 3d Task 1: quarantine_due, which alert_steps() writes daily, and quarantine_lost, which quarantine-record writes.
  "quarantine_due",
  "quarantine_lost",
  // 3d Task 2: release_undestroyed, which alert_steps() writes daily, and seal_released, which staffAlert writes after a release.
  "release_undestroyed",
  "seal_released",
  // 3d Task 3: edge_purge_failed, which the media module's job edge-purge writes as its own row, at most once in 24 hours.
  "edge_purge_failed",
  // 3d Task 5: head_unwitnessed and head_missed, which the transparency job writes as its own rows, each at most once in 24 hours.
  "head_unwitnessed",
  "head_missed",
  // 3d Task 6: automated_objection and automation_capped, which staffAlert writes after their commits, and
  // automated_waiting, which the automated sweep writes as its own row, at most once in 24 hours.
  "automated_objection",
  "automation_capped",
  "automated_waiting",
  // 3d Task 7: matcher_down, which alert_steps() writes daily and the first upload over the limit on refusals writes at
  // once, and hold_ended_unreported, which staffAlert writes after an end of a hold without a report.
  "matcher_down",
  "hold_ended_unreported",
  // 3d review M13: head_unmailed, which the transparency job writes as its own row, at most once in 24 hours.
  "head_unmailed",
  // 3b Task 5: import_image_flagged, which staffAlert writes after the import feeder's settling commit.
  "import_image_flagged",
];

/** A list of the contracts' words as a PostgreSQL array, for `= any(...)`: no word holds a comma or a quote. */
const words = (values: readonly string[]) => sql`${`{${values.join(",")}}`}::text[]`;

/**
 * The facts of an alert's push: the counts and times its kind names in ALERT_KINDS, never a handle, a lane's list or a
 * reason. 3c's and 3e's kinds keep their full message for the mail; the push gets these alone. A 3f alert's message is
 * its facts.
 */
export function alertFacts(message: StaffMessage): AlertFacts {
  switch (message.template) {
    case "moderation_urgent":
      // 3d review L8: the cases' count and oldest time, and the held uploads as a fact of their own when there are any.
      return { count: message.count, ...(message.oldest === null ? {} : { oldestAt: message.oldest.toISOString() }), ...(message.heldUploads ? { heldUploads: message.heldUploads } : {}) };
    case "moderation_waiting":
      // What the mail lists, each line's own count: the cases of each lane past its time, the cases that hold a measure
      // taken while deciding, and the replies waiting.
      return { count: message.lanes.reduce((sum, lane) => sum + Math.max(0, lane.count), 0) + message.interim + (message.replies?.count ?? 0) };
    case "moderation_burst":
      return { count: message.count };
    case "moderation_reads":
      return { limit: message.limit };
    case "moderation_reveal":
    case "moderation_csam_lifted":
      return { at: message.at.toISOString() };
    default:
      return message.facts;
  }
}

/** Writes one alert's row, with its kind's priority and scope; the database forces its times and its two legs as owed. */
async function insertAlert(q: Pick<ModerationDeps["apiDb"], "execute">, kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts): Promise<number> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const [row] = await q.execute<{ id: string }>(
    sql`insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts) values (${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${JSON.stringify(facts)}::jsonb) returning id`,
  );
  return Number(row!.id);
}

/**
 * Mails a 3f alert's row once: the row is taken FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED while its mail goes, and marked mailed when an
 * address took it, so staffAlert and the tick never both mail it. Answers how many addresses took it, or "elsewhere" when
 * another holds the row or it was mailed meanwhile.
 */
async function mailClaimed(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth">, id: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number | "elsewhere"> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const claimed = await tx.execute(sql`select id from public.alert_outbox where id = ${id} and mailed_at is null for update skip locked`);
    if (claimed.length === 0) return "elsewhere";
    const accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (accepted > 0) await tx.execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${id}`);
    return accepted;
  });
}

/**
 * 3d review L1: the row of the alert of a destructive act (an end of a hold without a report, a release), written inside
 * the act's own confirmed transaction before its audit row, as quarantine-record writes quarantine_lost: a restart after
 * the commit never loses it, since the watcher pushes the row and the alert tick mails a row left without its mail.
 * Without a throttle: each act is an alert of its own. Answers the row's id, for mailAlertRow after the commit.
 */
export function confirmedAlertRow(tx: Pick<ModerationDeps["apiDb"], "execute">, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number> {
  return insertAlert(tx, message.template, alertFacts(message));
}

/** 3d review L1: after the act's commit, the row's mail now, once; a failure is logged, and the alert tick mails the row. */
export async function mailAlertRow(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "log">, rowId: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await mailClaimed(deps, rowId, message);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its mail could not be sent now; the alert tick sends it");
  }
}

/**
 * Sends a staff alert at most once in its key's window (null: no throttle, for a reveal and for a decision that lifted
 * the protection of reported images). After the throttle, in this order: it writes the alert's row of alert_outbox, which
 * the watcher pushes; then it mails every staff account. For 3c's and 3e's kinds (`mail: "own"`) the mail is the caller's
 * full message, and the row is marked mailed whether or not an address took it: the tick never renders such a mail from
 * a row. For a kind of 3f whose mail is its sentence, the row is marked only when an address took the mail, and the tick
 * mails a row left without it.
 *
 * An alert fails open: a row that cannot be written is logged and the mail goes all the same, and when the store cannot
 * be reached both go without a throttle. It answers sent when either leg took the alert. The hit is given back, so the
 * next occasion that meets the alert's condition sends it again, when the mail of one of 3c's and 3e's kinds went to
 * nobody (no row can mail it later), and for a kind of 3f only when neither leg took it. A failed give-back is logged.
 * It never throws for a failed send, which mailStaff logs.
 */
export async function staffAlert(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log">, key: string | null, windowMs: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent"> {
  let counted = false;
  if (key !== null) {
    try {
      const hit = await deps.limits.hit(key, windowMs);
      counted = true;
      if (hit.count > 1) return "throttled";
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the limit store could not be reached; the alert goes without its throttle");
    }
  }
  const kind = message.template;
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  let rowId: number | null = null;
  try {
    // A statement of its own, in a savepoint where the caller holds a transaction: a refused row never aborts it.
    rowId = await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => insertAlert(tx, kind, alertFacts(message)));
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key ?? kind }, "moderation alert: its row for the phones could not be written; the mail goes all the same");
  }
  let accepted: number;
  if (entry.mail === "sentence" && rowId !== null) {
    const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, rowId, message).catch((err: unknown) => {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its mail could not be sent now; the alert tick sends it");
      return 0;
    });
    accepted = mailed === "elsewhere" ? 1 : mailed;
  } else {
    accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (rowId !== null && entry.mail === "own") {
      await deps.apiDb
        .execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${rowId}`)
        .catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its row could not be marked mailed; nothing mails it again"));
    }
  }
  const pushed = rowId !== null && entry.legs.includes("push");
  const giveBack = accepted === 0 && (entry.mail === "own" || !pushed);
  if (giveBack && counted && key !== null) {
    await deps.limits.release(key).catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the hit of an alert nobody received could not be given back"));
  }
  return accepted > 0 || pushed ? "sent" : "unsent";
}

/**
 * The urgent lane's alert: when an intake has put an item into lane 0, every staff account is told how many cases wait
 * there and since when the oldest does, and the phone on call is woken. A notice about a post that quotes another puts
 * two cases into the lane and sends one alert that counts both. Best effort, after the commit and the answer; the
 * dispatch job repeats it while a lane-0 item still calls for someone. 3d review L8 (people6): the held uploads that wait
 * are a fact of their own, never counted among the cases, and they alone send the alert when no case waits.
 */
export async function alertUrgentLane(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log" | "config"> & { media?: Pick<ModerationDeps["media"], "heldOverview"> }): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting"> {
  const waiting = await urgentWaiting(deps.apiDb);
  // 3d Task 7 (7.8 step 4, W.7): the held uploads no admin has ended, and those ended as report and not released on which
  // an objection waits, count beside the lane's cases, and the mail names them in a sentence of their own.
  const held = deps.media === undefined ? null : await deps.media.heldOverview();
  const heldUploads = held === null ? 0 : held.open + held.objected;
  // A case without a time cannot be one the lane holds open; the count and the time are the cases' alone.
  const cases = waiting.oldest === null ? 0 : waiting.count;
  // Decided in the moment between the intake's commit and this read: nothing is left to alert about.
  if (cases === 0 && heldUploads === 0) return "nothing_waiting";
  // 3f's review (people4): the mail says whether the phone on call got the push, or that it is the only alert.
  return staffAlert(deps, URGENT_ALERT_KEY, URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, {
    template: "moderation_urgent",
    count: cases,
    oldest: cases === 0 ? null : waiting.oldest,
    phones: deps.config.NOTIFY !== "off",
    ...(heldUploads > 0 ? { heldUploads } : {}),
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the channel's health

/** The alert channel's state as the console's home and the tick read it, with the time since when. */
export interface ChannelHealth {
  channel: AlertChannelState;
  since: Date | null;
}

/**
 * The channel's state, read fresh (3f design, sections 5 and 7.2 step 3), by the database's clock: `off` with NOTIFY=off;
 * `down` while the watcher's beat is older than channel_down_minutes (or there never was one), or a row still owed its
 * push (a kind with a push leg, not pushed, younger than push_owed_minutes) is older than that while no publish has
 * worked for as long (push_ok_at; 3f's review, operations3: rows waiting behind ntfy's request limit, which answers and
 * takes some every round, never read as down, and Home never says that alerts arrive by mail only then); `mailbox`
 * while the beat is fresh and the mailbox was last read longer ago than that; `ok` otherwise. A row past its push's
 * bound counts for nothing any more, so the state clears by itself once the push server is back. `since` is the earliest
 * late time, or the clock's when there is none (a watcher that never beat, a mailbox never read).
 */
export async function channelHealth(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">): Promise<ChannelHealth> {
  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "off") return { channel: "off", since: null };
  const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ now: string; beat_at: string | null; mailbox_ok_at: string | null; owed_since: string | null; beat_late: boolean; owed_late: boolean; mailbox_late: boolean }>(sql`
    select now() as now, s.beat_at, s.mailbox_ok_at, o.owed_since,
           (s.beat_at is null or s.beat_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as beat_late,
           coalesce(o.owed_since < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes), false)
             and (s.push_ok_at is null or s.push_ok_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as owed_late,
           (s.mailbox_ok_at is null or s.mailbox_ok_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as mailbox_late
      from public.order_rules() r
      left join public.notify_state s on s.id = 1
      cross join lateral (select min(x.created_at) as owed_since from public.alert_outbox x
                           where x.pushed_at is null and x.kind = any(${words(PUSH_KINDS)})
                             and x.created_at > now() - make_interval(mins => r.push_owed_minutes)) o`);
  const at = (value: string | null) => (value === null ? null : new Date(value));
  const now = new Date(row!.now);
  if (row!.beat_late || row!.owed_late) {
    const late = [row!.beat_late ? at(row!.beat_at) : null, row!.owed_late ? at(row!.owed_since) : null].filter((d): d is Date => d !== null);
    return { channel: "down", since: late.length === 0 ? now : new Date(Math.min(...late.map((d) => d.getTime()))) };
  }
  if (row!.mailbox_late) return { channel: "mailbox", since: at(row!.mailbox_ok_at) ?? now };
  return { channel: "ok", since: null };
}

/**
 * The tick's own alarm: one row of `alert_channel_down` (mailed only) or `mailbox_unreachable` (pushed and mailed), at
 * most once in 24 hours by the outbox's own rows, with no key in the limit store. Answers whether it wrote one.
 */
async function raiseAlarm(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, kind: "alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable", since: Date): Promise<boolean> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const facts = JSON.stringify({ since: since.toISOString() });
  const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute(sql`
    insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
    select ${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${facts}::jsonb
     where not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox o where o.kind = ${kind} and o.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
    returning id`);
  return rows.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the alert tick

export interface TickReport {
  /** How many rows alert_steps() wrote, or null when the step failed. */
  steps: number | null;
  /** The channel's state, or null when NOTIFY is off or the step failed. */
  channel: AlertChannelState | null;
  /** The alarms the round raised. */
  raised: ("alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable")[];
}

/**
 * One round of the alert tick (3f design, section 7.2), each step in a try of its own:
 *   1. `select alert_steps()`: the database writes every time-driven row that is due;
 *   2. the channel's health, skipped with NOTIFY=off: its alarm rows, which the mail leg mails.
 * The mail leg (section 7.2's step 2) is alertMailLeg, a job of its own since 3f's review (ALERT_MAIL_JOB).
 */
export async function alertTick(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "log">): Promise<TickReport> {
  const report: TickReport = { steps: null, channel: null, raised: [] };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_TICK_JOB, step: name }, "alert-tick: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };

  await step("steps", async () => {
    const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ written: number }>(sql`select public.alert_steps() as written`);
    report.steps = Number(row!.written);
  });

  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "on") {
    await step("channel", async () => {
      const health = await channelHealth(deps);
      report.channel = health.channel;
      if (health.channel === "down" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "alert_channel_down", health.since!))) report.raised.push("alert_channel_down");
      if (health.channel === "mailbox" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "mailbox_unreachable", health.since!))) report.raised.push("mailbox_unreachable");
    });
  }
  return report;
}

/**
 * One round of the mail leg (3f design, section 7.2 step 2): every row of a kind whose mail is its sentence, not yet
 * mailed and younger than ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours, whoever wrote it, mailed to every staff account and marked when an
 * address took it; a row nobody took is tried again next round, and then left. Each row in a try of its own. It never
 * mails a row of 3c's or 3e's kinds: their mails say more than the row's facts, and staffAlert sends them. Answers how
 * many rows it mailed.
 */
export async function alertMailLeg(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "log">): Promise<number> {
  let mailedRows = 0;
  try {
    const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ id: string; kind: StaffAlertKind; facts: AlertFacts }>(sql`
      select id, kind, facts from public.alert_outbox
       where mailed_at is null and kind = any(${words(TICK_MAILED_KINDS)})
         and created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => ${ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours})
       order by id`);
    for (const row of rows) {
      try {
        const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, Number(row.id), { template: row.kind, facts: row.facts });
        if (typeof mailed === "number" && mailed > 0) mailedRows++;
        else if (mailed === 0) deps.log.warn({ job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, alert: row.id, kind: row.kind }, "alert-mail: no staff address took an alert's mail; it is tried again next round");
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, alert: row.id }, "alert-mail: an alert's mail failed; it is tried again next round");
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB }, "alert-mail: the rows owed their mail could not be read; the next round reads them again");
  }
  return mailedRows;
}

/** The alert tick as a job of the shared lock: a round ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended, on one instance at a time. */
export function createAlertTick(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: ALERT_TICK_JOB, intervalMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => alertTick(deps) });
}

/** The mail leg as a job of the shared lock under a key of its own, at the tick's interval, so a slow relay holds only it. */
export function createAlertMailJob(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, intervalMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => alertMailLeg(deps) });
}
```

```ts
/** What the staff module needs from this one: the console's operations on cases, which its routes run behind the staff gate. */
export interface ModerationForStaff {

  contact(query: ContactQuery): Promise<ContactPage>;

  closeContact(session: ActiveStaffSession, messageId: string, request: ContactCloseRequest, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<void>;

  orders(): Promise<OrdersPage>;

  order(session: ActiveStaffSession, orderId: string): Promise<OrderView | null>;

  openOrder(session: ActiveStaffSession, request: OrderOpenRequest, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<OrderView>;

  addOrderItems(session: ActiveStaffSession, orderId: string, request: OrderItemsRequest, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<OrderView>;

  recordOrderEvent(session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<OrderOutcome>;

  correctOrder(session: ActiveStaffSession, orderId: string, facts: OrderCorrectFacts, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed | null, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<OrderOutcome | "step_up_required">;

  giveOrderEffect(session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<OrderOutcome>;

/**
 * What the social module needs from this one (3c design, section 5): the facts behind the chip on the author's own post.

 */
export interface ModerationForSocial {
  authorFacts(viewer: string, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostModeration>>;
  /**
   * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 and 7.9): createPost calls this after its commit when the post has images. It starts the
   * automated step of each image whose score is at or over the threshold on the module's background and returns at once,
   * so a post never waits for a deciding transaction; with the scorer off it starts nothing.
   */
  imagesPublished(postId: string): void;
}

/**
 * What the imports module needs from this one (3b design, section 8.1; Task 5): the staff alert for imported images whose
 * match does not act, which an import leaves out and never publishes. Task 6 adds imagesPublished for imported posts.

export interface ModerationForImports {
  /**
   * After the commit that left `count` images of import `importId` out as flagged: the alert import_image_flagged to every
   * staff account, its facts the time and the count alone, at most once an hour an import (IMPORT_FLAGGED_WINDOW_MS); a
   * later occasion within the hour is throttled, as automation_capped's are. Never throws.
   */
  imagesFlagged(input: { importId: string; count: number; at: Date }): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent">;
}

/** The throttle of import_image_flagged: one alert an hour an import. */
export const IMPORT_FLAGGED_WINDOW_MS = 60 * 60_000;

/** What the account module needs from this one (3c design, sections 5, 7.10 and 7.11): the purge's forgetting, and the export's member; 3e adds the take-down of terminated accounts. */
export interface ModerationForAccount {
  /**
   * Forgets that a deleted account sent its reports: the account's id goes from its intakes and their items, which go on
   * being processed. The database acts only on an account whose auth row the take-down marked deleted, and changes
   * nothing when run again.

  forgetAccount(userId: string): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * The moderation member of the account's data export: the decisions about the account that its Cases screen lists and
   * its own reports and notices while their records are kept, each as the account's own screens show it. Never another

  exportFor(userId: string): Promise<ModerationExport>;

   * Answers how many it took down and how many failed; one failure never stops the next account.
   */
  takeDownDue(takeDown: TakeDown): Promise<{ terminated: number; failed: number }>;
}

export interface CreateModerationOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The auth module's interface for moderation: auth.forModeration. */
  auth: AuthForModeration;
  /** The social module's interface for cases: socialForModeration(apiDb). */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  /** The media module's interface for cases: media.forCases. */
  media: MediaForCases;
  /**
   * The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. The author's and the reporter's
   * routes stand behind it. Without it they refuse every request, so a module built for the staff side alone opens none.
   */
  requireSession?: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** What one sender may send, and the throttles of the staff alerts, count in the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createModeration(options: CreateModerationOptions) {
  const deps: ModerationDeps = {
    apiDb: options.apiDb,
    auth: options.auth,
    social: options.social,
    media: options.media,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    background: createBackground(options.logger),
    config: options.config,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  const forStaff: ModerationForStaff = {
    decide: (session, confirmed, ctx) => decide(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    decidedCase: (session, caseId) => readDecidedCase(deps, session, caseId),
    review: (session, confirmed, ctx) => review(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    reviewedCase: async (session, decisionId) => readDecidedCase(deps, session, await reviewedCase(deps, decisionId)),
    appeals: (session, cursor) => appealsList(deps, session, cursor),
    overview: (session) => overview(deps, session),
    queue: (cursor) => queue(deps, cursor),
    standing: () => standingLists(deps.apiDb),
    caseView: (session, caseId) => readCase(deps, session, caseId),
    caseImage: (session, caseId, mediaId, size) => caseImage(deps, session, caseId, mediaId, size),
    takeSnapshot: (session, caseId) => takeSnapshot(deps, session, caseId),
    openFinding: (session, request) => openFinding(deps, session, request),
    saveText: (session, caseId, request) => saveText(deps, session, caseId, request),
    texts: (session, caseId) => ownTexts(deps, session, caseId),
    reveal: (session, confirmed, ctx) => reveal(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    contact: (query) => contactPage(deps, query),
    closeContact: (session, messageId, request, ctx) => closeContact(deps, session, messageId, request, ctx),
    orders: () => ordersPage(deps),
    order: (session, orderId) => orderView(deps, orderId, session),
    openOrder: (session, request, ctx) => openOrder(deps, session, request, ctx),
    addOrderItems: (session, orderId, request, ctx) => addItems(deps, session, orderId, request, ctx),
    recordOrderEvent: (session, confirmed, ctx) => recordEvent(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    correctOrder: (session, orderId, facts, confirmed, ctx) => correctOrderRecord(deps, session, orderId, facts, confirmed, ctx),
    giveOrderEffect: (session, confirmed, ctx) => giveEffect(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    restore: () => restoreView(deps),
    closeGap: (session, confirmed, ctx) => closeGapNotNeeded(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    release: (session, confirmed, ctx) => releaseSeal(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    uploads: (session, cursor) => heldUploads(deps, session, cursor),
    endHold: (session, confirmed, ctx) => endHold(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    releaseUpload: (session, confirmed, ctx) => releaseUpload(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    copyTaken: async (facts) => {
      // Started and not waited for, as what follows a decision is: the download's answer never waits for a mail relay.
      deps.background.start(async () => {
        try {
          await staffAlert(deps, null, 0, { template: "copy_taken", facts });
        } catch (err) {
          deps.log.error({ err }, "moderation: the staff accounts were not alerted to a download of the audit log's tail");
        }
      });
    },
  };
  const forSocial: ModerationForSocial = {
    authorFacts: (viewer, postIds) => authorFacts(deps, viewer, postIds),
    imagesPublished: (postId) => imagesPublished(deps, postId),
  };
  const forImports: ModerationForImports = {
    async imagesFlagged({ importId, count, at }) {
      try {
        return await staffAlert(deps, `import-image-flagged:${importId}`, IMPORT_FLAGGED_WINDOW_MS, { template: "import_image_flagged", facts: { at: at.toISOString(), count } });
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, count }, "moderation: the staff accounts were not alerted to imported images left out as flagged");
        return "unsent";
      }
    },
  };
  const forAccount: ModerationForAccount = {
    forgetAccount: async (userId) => {
      await forgetReporter(deps.apiDb, userId);
    },
    exportFor: (userId) => exportFor(deps, userId),
    takeDownDue: (takeDown) => takeDownDue(deps, takeDown),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /**
     * The app's routes, mounted at /api: reports and notices, their status page with its contact buttons and its
     * re-examinations, and behind the session guard the account's own decisions, appeals, reports and re-examinations.
     */
    routes: moderationRoutes(deps, options.requireSession ?? noSession),
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
    /** The interface the social module's views use. */
    forSocial,
    /** The interface the account module's purge and export use. */
    forAccount,
    /** 3b Task 5: the interface the imports module uses. */
    forImports,
    /**
     * 3d Task 7 (design, section 5): the handler the wiring hands the media module (media.onMatch), which it calls after
     * the commit of a refusal, of a match on a posted image, and of an upload over the limit on refusals.
     */
    matched: matchedHandler(deps),
    /**
     * 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me's standing, read fresh from the ledger: null for an account without a live
     * profile. The app composes the route from this and the auth module's meFor.
     */
    standingFor: (userId: string) => standingFor(deps.apiDb, userId),
    /**
     * Resolves once every task a request started and did not wait for has ended: the mails after a report, a notice, a
     * finding, a reveal or a refused case read. The tests await it; the server lets the tasks run.
     */
    settle: () => deps.background.settle(),
    /**
     * Starts the module's background work under the jobs' shared lock, on one API instance at a time: the dispatch job
     * and 3f's alert tick and its mail leg (two jobs since 3f's review, so a slow relay never holds the tick) always, (3d
     * Task 6) the automated sweep always, whose reads of signals each run only while their tool is on, and the retention
     * job always. The dispatch and retention jobs' first rounds come ten minutes after the start, the tick's 30 seconds
     * after it. While MODERATION_RETENTION is off the retention job's rounds run one step alone (3d Task 8, design section
     * 7.14): tools_off, which forgets the hashes and the ratings of a tool that is off and is held by nothing but that
     * tool's setting; nothing else is erased, released or deleted, and the warning is logged at every start, so a switch
     * left off after a restore is seen. The tick runs all the same, since an alert is never about retention. Answers the
     * function that stops them all; a round in flight finishes.
     */
    startJobs: (lock: JobLock): (() => void) => {
      const stopDispatch = createDispatchJob(deps, lock).start();
      const stopTick = createAlertTick(deps, lock).start();
      const stopMail = createAlertMailJob(deps, lock).start();
      const stopSweep = createAutomatedSweepJob(deps, lock).start();
      if (deps.config.MODERATION_RETENTION !== "on") deps.log.warn(RETENTION_OFF_WARNING);
      const stopRetention = createRetentionJob(deps, lock).start();
      return () => {
        stopDispatch();
        stopTick();
        stopMail();
        stopSweep();
        stopRetention();
      };
    },
  };
}

export type Moderation = ReturnType<typeof createModeration>;
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { AltText, MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST } from "./media";
import { FORBIDDEN_CONTROL, FORBIDDEN_FORMAT, normalizePostBody, postLength, visibleLength } from "./text";

/**
 * Import from other platforms (3b design, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-import-3b-design.md, sections 5.1 and 9.3;
 * Task 1): the line the importer writes and the API reads back as hostile input, the importer's summary, the intake's
 * numbers, the person's choice, the views, the closed lists and every number of the design. It imports only zod,
 * ./media and ./text, so social.ts, moderation.ts, staff.ts and account.ts can read ImportSource while they load.
 */

const rules = {
  /** 7.3: a chunk is exactly this long but the last; under Cloudflare's 100 MB and inside its 125-second read timeout. */
  chunkBytes: 8_388_608,
  /** 7.3: the largest archive, 256 chunks; the CHECK of import_jobs.declared_bytes (6.1). */
  maxBytes: 2_147_483_648,
  /** 7.3: Caddy's body limit for a chunk, its "9MB", which Caddy reads as decimal megabytes. */
  chunkBodyBytes: 9_000_000,
  /** 9.4: the app sends a chunk whose hash differed again at most this often. */
  chunkRetries: 3,
  /** 4.2 step 3, decision 21: an account imports once it is this old (import_too_soon). */
  minAccountAgeDays: 7,
  /** Decision 21: an account younger than this publishes at most newAccountMaxPosts posts per import. */
  newAccountDays: 30,
  newAccountMaxPosts: 1_000,
  /** 7.6: the limits. Published imports per account in seven days, imports created per address in a day, and per hour per account. */
  importsPerWeek: 3,
  importsPerAddressDay: 5,
  chunksPerHour: 600,
  actsPerHour: 20,
  picksPerHour: 3_000,
  /** 7.7: the default of IMPORT_MAX_ACTIVE, imports in uploading or scanning on the site at once. */
  maxActiveDefault: 2,
  /** 7.4, 7.7: IMPORT_IMAGES_PER_HOUR's default, and the most it may be set to (it may only be lowered). */
  imagesPerHourDefault: 600,
  imagesPerHourMax: 600,
  /** 7.7: the default of IMPORT_MIN_FREE_BYTES, kept free on import-archives beyond a new import's size and scanWriteBytes. */
  minFreeBytesDefault: 2_147_483_648,
  /** 4.2 step 3, 7.2: the most a scan may write to import-work. */
  scanWriteBytes: 4_294_967_296,
  /** 7.1: the importer rewrites its heartbeat this often; the API takes no new import once it is older than the second. */
  heartbeatMs: 10_000,
  heartbeatStaleMs: 60_000,
  /** 4.8, decision 4: an archive lives at most this long after its import was created (an upload not complete then expires, a scan not done fails). */
  archiveHours: 24,
  /** 4.8: a scan not done this long after the upload ended fails (scan_timed_out). */
  scanMinutes: 45,
  /** 4.8: a preview not confirmed this long after the scan ended expires. */
  previewHours: 24,
  /** 4.8, decision 19: an imported image whose check is not answered this long after its upload is left out. */
  checkHours: 24,
  /** 4.8: an import not finished this long after its scan ended is stopped; the work folder never outlives it (the terms' three days). */
  workHours: 72,
  /** 4.8, decision 25: a finished import's record stays at least this long after its end. */
  recordDays: 30,
  /** 5.3 step 7, decision 13: a longer text is skipped (too_long_to_read). */
  textMax: 30_000,
  /** Decision 13: a post over this many code points is long; shortened, it is cut to this many with its ellipsis. */
  shortenTo: 1_000,
  /** 5.4: items read, posts kept and images kept by one scan. */
  maxItems: 1_000_000,
  maxPosts: 50_000,
  maxImages: 5_000,
  /** 5.4: a date before the first tweet, or more than futureDays after the import was created, is skipped (date_out_of_range). */
  earliestDate: "2006-03-21",
  futureDays: 1,
  /** 5.5, 5.6: one JSON element of a data file, in bytes and levels (item_too_large). */
  itemMaxBytes: 1_048_576,
  itemMaxDepth: 64,
  /** 5.5: X's data/manifest.js, and the highest N of data/tweets-part<N>.js. */
  manifestMaxBytes: 1_048_576,
  tweetsPartsMax: 99,
  /** 5.7: a CAR's blocks, and its MST's levels and entries a node. */
  carBlockMaxBytes: 1_000_000,
  carMaxBlocks: 2_000_000,
  mstMaxDepth: 48,
  mstMaxEntries: 4_096,
  /** 7.2: the zip reader's limits: entries, central directory, a name, a data file, the ratio, the allowlisted entries' sum. */
  zipMaxEntries: 200_000,
  zipDirectoryMaxBytes: 67_108_864,
  zipNameMaxBytes: 512,
  zipDataMaxBytes: 1_073_741_824,
  zipMaxRatio: 100,
  zipTotalMaxBytes: 4_294_967_296,
  /** 7.1, 7.5: the file protocol's caps: job.json, summary.json, a line of posts.jsonl, and posts.jsonl (whose lines are at most maxPosts). */
  jobFileMaxBytes: 4_096,
  summaryMaxBytes: 65_536,
  lineMaxBytes: 262_144,
  postsFileMaxBytes: 1_073_741_824,
  /** 7.1: the third start of a scan fails it (interrupted); the watchdog ends a scan; the loop sleeps this long when idle. */
  maxAttempts: 3,
  watchdogMs: 1_800_000,
  idleMs: 1_000,
  /** 6.1: the CHECKs of import_jobs (refused_words in code points, scan and choice in bytes), import_picks.alts, import_keys.key and the seed. */
  refusedWordsMax: 80,
  scanMaxBytes: 262_144,
  choiceMaxBytes: 1_024,
  altsMaxBytes: 16_384,
  keyBytes: 32,
  seedBytes: 32,
  /** 7.4: imported images in processing on the site at once. */
  imagesInFlight: 2,
  /** 7.5: import-drive's interval and lock, the intake's batch of keys, a batch of posts, batches a round, the orphan pass. */
  driveIntervalMs: 5_000,
  driveLockMs: 60_000,
  keyBatch: 1_000,
  batchPosts: 200,
  publishBatchesPerRound: 10,
  undoBatchesPerRound: 5,
  orphanEveryRounds: 10,
  orphanAgeMs: 3_600_000,
  /** 9.2: lines a page of the preview, pages kept, samples and a sample's bytes, imports listed. */
  pageLines: 50,
  maxPages: 1_000,
  samples: 3,
  sampleMaxBytes: 262_144,
  listMax: 20,
};

/**
 * Every number of the design (section 9.3), as 3d's AUTOMATION_RULES holds its own: the CHECK constants of Task 2's
 * migrations mirror the ones of 6.1, a database test holds them equal, and the terms print their hours and days from
 * here (11.3). Settings that the owner may change are named for their defaults.
 */
export const IMPORT_RULES: Readonly<typeof rules> = rules;

export const IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS = ["x", "mastodon", "bluesky"] as const;
export const ImportSource = z.enum(IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS);
export type ImportSource = z.infer<typeof ImportSource>;

/** The twelve states of section 4.1. */
export const ImportStatus = z.enum(["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing", "done", "stopped", "undoing", "undone", "failed", "cancelled", "expired"]);
export type ImportStatus = z.infer<typeof ImportStatus>;

/** The active states: an account has at most one import in them (import_jobs_one_active). undoing is not one. */
export const IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES = ["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing"] as const satisfies readonly ImportStatus[];

/** Why a scan failed: import_jobs.failure's CHECK, and a failed summary's member. */
export const IMPORT_FAILURES = [
  "not_this_source",
  "not_an_archive",
  "tar_gz",
  "partial_archive",
  "encrypted",
  "too_many_entries",
  "too_large_uncompressed",
  "bad_entry_name",
  "unreadable",
  "nothing_to_import",
  "scan_timed_out",
  "interrupted",
] as const;
export const ImportFailure = z.enum(IMPORT_FAILURES);
export type ImportFailure = z.infer<typeof ImportFailure>;

/** Why an import was stopped: import_jobs.stop_reason's CHECK. */
export const IMPORT_STOP_REASONS = ["refused_image", "by_author", "by_staff", "time_ran_out"] as const;
export type ImportStopReason = (typeof IMPORT_STOP_REASONS)[number];

/**
 * Why a post is not published. reply, too_long, warning, protected and left_out are counted by the app from the month
 * table and the picks when the choice leaves them out; already_imported and new_account_cap by the intake; the rest by
 * the importer.
 */
export const IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS = [
  "repost",
  "reply",
  "too_long",
  "warning",
  "protected",
  "left_out",
  "not_public",
  "older_version",
  "poll",
  "adult_label",
  "too_long_to_read",
  "date_out_of_range",
  "item_too_large",
  "unreadable",
  "empty",
  "already_imported",
  "over_post_cap",
  "over_item_cap",
  "new_account_cap",
] as const;
export type ImportSkipReason = (typeof IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS)[number];

/** Why an image is not imported. */
export const IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS = ["video", "sensitive", "unsupported", "too_large", "missing_file", "bluesky_no_files", "images_off", "not_chosen", "no_description", "over_image_cap", "failed", "not_checked", "flagged"] as const;
export type ImportImageSkip = (typeof IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS)[number];

/**
 * A line's marks, the facts a choice decides on, as bits: IMPORT_MARKS[i] is the bit 1 << i. reply: its kind is reply;
 * long: its text is over shortenTo code points; warning and protected: the line's members of those names.
 */
export const IMPORT_MARKS = ["reply", "long", "warning", "protected"] as const;

const Count = z.int().min(0);
const Ref = z.int().min(0).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts - 1);
/** A byte offset into posts.jsonl. */
const Offset = z.int().min(0).max(IMPORT_RULES.postsFileMaxBytes);
const Marks = z.int().min(0).max(2 ** IMPORT_MARKS.length - 1);
const Month = z.string().regex(/^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/);
/** The archive's day, never its second, which with the text would fingerprint the original. */
const Day = z.iso.date();
const Kind = z.enum(["post", "thread", "reply"]);

/**
 * PostText's rule with textMax in place of POST_MAX_LENGTH, and its raw cap scaled the same way (four UTF-16 units a code
 * point). This module's refinements carry no message of their own: no person reads them (the API answers invalid_request
 * and the intake counts a line unreadable), and every byte here is in the app's web bundle.
 */
export const ImportedText = z
  .string()
  .max(IMPORT_RULES.textMax * 4)
  .transform(normalizePostBody)
  .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_CONTROL.test(text))
  .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text))
  .refine((text) => postLength(text) <= IMPORT_RULES.textMax);
export type ImportedText = z.infer<typeof ImportedText>;

/**
 * The only names the work folder's media/ may hold: <ref>-<position>.<jpg|png|webp>, the ref without leading zeros and
 * below maxPosts, the position from 0, as refs count, and below MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST (so 0 to 3).
 */
export const ImportMediaFile = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})-[0-3][.](jpg|png|webp)$/)
  .refine((file) => Number.parseInt(file, 10) < IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts);
export type ImportMediaFile = z.infer<typeof ImportMediaFile>;

/** One kept post, one line of posts.jsonl (5.1). The importer writes it; the API parses every line with this schema. */
export const ImportedPost = z
  .strictObject({
    /** Its line in posts.jsonl, from 0; lines are in ascending order of `at`. */
    ref: Ref,
    /** HMAC-SHA256 of the source and the source post's id under the account's import key, as 64 lowercase hex. */
    key: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/),
    /** The date the archive gives the post, UTC, whole seconds. */
    at: z.iso.datetime({ offset: false, precision: 0 }),
    /** post: the account's own top-level post; thread: a reply to its own post; reply: a reply to someone else. */
    kind: Kind,
    /** The ref of the post a `thread` item answers, always lower than its own ref; null otherwise. */
    parent: z.int().min(0).nullable(),
    /** korbat's plain text: converted, cleaned and normalised (5.3); up to textMax code points. */
    text: ImportedText,
    /** Images in the work folder, in order; `alt` is the source's description, normalised, or null. */
    media: z.array(z.strictObject({ file: ImportMediaFile, alt: AltText.nullable() })).max(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST),
    /** X only: dated inside a period protected-history.js marks as protected (5.5); left out unless chosen. */
    protected: z.boolean(),
    /** Mastodon only: the text begins with a content warning's line (decision 12); left out unless chosen. */
    warning: z.boolean(),
  })
  .refine((post) => (post.kind === "thread") === (post.parent !== null) && (post.parent === null || post.parent < post.ref), { path: ["parent"] })
  .refine((post) => visibleLength(post.text) >= 1 || post.media.length >= 1, { path: ["text"] })
  .refine(
    (post) => {
      const names = post.media.map(({ file }) => file.split(/[-.]/));
      return names.every(([ref]) => Number(ref) === post.ref) && new Set(names.map(([, position]) => position)).size === names.length;
    },
    { path: ["media"] },
  );
export type ImportedPost = z.infer<typeof ImportedPost>;

/** The counts a scan reports and the intake keeps: counts only, every reason from the closed lists. */
const scanCounts = {
  /** Lines written (the summary), or lines the preview offers (the intake: readable, not already imported, not over the new account's cap). */
  posts: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts),
  images: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxImages),
  skipped: z.partialRecord(z.enum(IMPORT_SKIP_REASONS), Count),
  imagesSkipped: z.partialRecord(z.enum(IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS), Count),
  /** Characters removed by 5.3 step 5, and descriptions that became null. */
  cleaned: Count,
  /** Posts that begin with a content warning's line (Mastodon), and links to the source platform replaced by words (5.3 step 3b). */
  warnings: Count,
  sourceLinks: Count,
  /** X posts dated inside a protected period. */
  protectedPosts: Count,
  /** The scan stopped at maxItems (over_item_cap). */
  readInPart: z.boolean(),
};

/** summary.json, the importer's last write for a scan and its commit point (7.1 step 4). The API parses it as hostile input. */
export const ImportSummary = z.discriminatedUnion("status", [
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("scanned"), ...scanCounts }),
  z.strictObject({ v: z.literal(1), id: z.uuid(), status: z.literal("failed"), failure: ImportFailure }),
]);
export type ImportSummary = z.infer<typeof ImportSummary>;

/**
 * A month table: per month, one group per set of marks that occurs, as [marks, posts, images, imagesUndescribed]. In the
 * scan: the lines the preview offers, their images, and those of their images without a source's description. In the
 * picks' counts: [marks, posts left out, images with a source's description in posts left out, images given a
 * description by a pick in posts not left out], so the app's totals stay exact.
 */
const MonthTable = z.array(z.object({ month: Month, groups: z.array(z.tuple([Marks, Count, Count, Count])).max(2 ** IMPORT_MARKS.length) }));

/**
 * What the intake stores in import_jobs.scan (6.1, 7.5 step 2). `fromRef` is the lowest ref that may be published (a
 * new account's newest lines only); `samples` the three newest lines' refs and byte offsets; `pages` every pageLines-th
 * line's byte offset. The move out of ready keeps the counts and fromRef and empties the rest. 3b Task 5 (the
 * orchestrator's ruling): the confirmation adds `chosen`, the posts and images the person's choice holds, counted from
 * the month table and the picks as the app counts them before the table is cut; the progress's totals read it.
 */
export const ImportScanFacts = z.object({
  ...scanCounts,
  months: MonthTable,
  first: Month.nullable(),
  last: Month.nullable(),
  fromRef: Ref,
  samples: z.array(z.object({ ref: Ref, offset: Offset })).max(IMPORT_RULES.samples),
  pages: z.array(Offset).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPages),
  chosen: z.object({ posts: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxPosts), images: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxImages) }).optional(),
});
export type ImportScanFacts = z.infer<typeof ImportScanFacts>;

/** The person's choice (4.4): a range of months, inclusive, either end open when null; never `from` after `to`. */
export const ImportChoice = z
  .strictObject({
    from: Month.nullable(),
    to: Month.nullable(),
    replies: z.boolean(),
    warnings: z.boolean(),
    protected: z.boolean(),
    images: z.boolean(),
    long: z.enum(["leave", "shorten"]),
  })
  .refine((choice) => choice.from === null || choice.to === null || choice.from <= choice.to, { path: ["to"] });
export type ImportChoice = z.infer<typeof ImportChoice>;

/** One line of the preview's list (9.2), with the person's pick: `alts[i]` is the description written for media[i]. */
export const ImportLineView = z.object({
  ref: Ref,
  at: Day,
  kind: Kind,
  marks: Marks,
  text: z.string(),
  media: z.array(z.object({ file: ImportMediaFile, alt: z.string().nullable() })),
  leftOut: z.boolean(),
  alts: z.array(z.string().nullable()),
});
export type ImportLineView = z.infer<typeof ImportLineView>;

/** A pick (4.4): leave the line out or not, and a description for each image its source gave none, by position in media. */
export const ImportPickRequest = z.strictObject({ leftOut: z.boolean(), alts: z.array(AltText.nullable()).max(MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST) });
export type ImportPickRequest = z.infer<typeof ImportPickRequest>;

/** The pick as saved, and the picks' counts by month and marks. */
export const ImportPickView = z.object({ ref: Ref, leftOut: z.boolean(), alts: z.array(z.string().nullable()), picks: MonthTable });
export type ImportPickView = z.infer<typeof ImportPickView>;

export const CreateImportRequest = z.strictObject({ source: ImportSource, bytes: z.int().min(1).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes) });
export type CreateImportRequest = z.infer<typeof CreateImportRequest>;

/** The statement (decision 14) is part of the request: without it there is nothing to confirm. */
export const ConfirmImportRequest = z.strictObject({ choice: ImportChoice, statement: z.literal(true) });
export type ConfirmImportRequest = z.infer<typeof ConfirmImportRequest>;

/**
 * An import as its owner sees it (9.3). No text but the samples (only in ready) and the refused post's first words, no
 * file name, no source id. `scan` holds the facts without their offsets; `endedByStaff` is the rule's id when an admin
 * ended it; `refusedAt` is the archive's day of the post whose image was refused.
 */
export const ImportView = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  source: ImportSource,
  status: ImportStatus,
  createdAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  endedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  declaredBytes: z.int().min(1).max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes),
  receivedBytes: Count.max(IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes),
  chunkBytes: z.int().min(1),
  failure: ImportFailure.nullable(),
  stopReason: z.enum(IMPORT_STOP_REASONS).nullable(),
  endedByStaff: z.string().nullable(),
  scan: ImportScanFacts.omit({ samples: true, pages: true }).nullable(),
  samples: z.array(z.object({ at: Day, text: z.string() })).max(IMPORT_RULES.samples),
  choice: ImportChoice.nullable(),
  picks: MonthTable,
  /**
   * 3b Task 5 (the orchestrator's ruling): `imagesLeftOut` holds the images the preparation left out, by reason (the job's
   * images_left_out_by), whose counts sum to the settled images that were not kept, for the result's notice.
   */
  progress: z.object({
    imagesTotal: Count,
    imagesSettled: Count,
    postsTotal: Count,
    postsPublished: Count,
    postsRemoved: Count,
    postsLeft: Count,
    imagesLeftOut: z.partialRecord(z.enum(IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS), Count),
  }),
  paused: z.boolean(),
  refusalId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  refusedAt: Day.nullable(),
  refusedWords: z.string().nullable(),
  undoable: z.boolean(),
});
export type ImportView = z.infer<typeof ImportView>;

/**
 * Every code the imports endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code; rate_limited, account_suspended and not_found are shared.
 * import_weekly_limit is the account's three published imports in seven days (import-week), a code of its own so the app
 * says that and not the per-address limit's words, which rate_limited carries (the orchestrator's ruling for Task 4).
 */
export const ImportErrorCode = z.enum([
  "imports_unavailable",
  "import_active",
  "rate_limited",
  "import_weekly_limit",
  "archive_too_large",
  "wrong_state",
  "wrong_offset",
  "chunk_too_large",
  "chunk_mismatch",
  "not_an_archive",
  "statement_required",
  "nothing_chosen",
  "import_too_soon",
  "account_suspended",
  "not_found",
]);
export type ImportErrorCode = z.infer<typeof ImportErrorCode>;
```

```ts
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

// imports nothing from the other modules of the contracts but text.ts, which imports nothing, and (3d Task 3) media.ts,
// which imports only text.ts, for the edge's numbers and the purge line of an order's item: moderation.ts reads its
// constants for the staff overview, staff.ts its step-up params, and the watcher (apps/api/src/notify), which imports the
// contracts and nothing of the API, renders its pushes from it.

 * The numbers of 3f, the same as the SQL function order_rules() returns, which a database test compares member by
 * member: one constant mirrors one function, as STANDING_RULES mirrors standing_rules(). Every function and view of 3f
 * reads its numbers from there, and every word of the console, the pushes and the mails from here. Each is a cautious
 * default flagged for the owner (3f design, section 2): one line to change in each place.
 */

  hourMinutes: 60,

  targetMinutes: 55,

  holdDays: 43,
  holdExtensionDays: 42,

  holdWarningDays: 7,
  /** No shorter hold for a tick the command line has not confirmed; a number here would cap it. */
  unconfirmedHoldHours: null,
  /** How long what a removal order disabled is preserved: months from the disabling, and a margin of days. */
  preserveMonths: 6,

  quietMinutes: 15,

} as const;
export type OrderRules = typeof ORDER_RULES;

/** What the database never reads: the watcher's round, the alert tick's, and how long the tick tries a row's mail. */
export const ALERT_RULES = {

  tickSeconds: 30,

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 7.1 and 8.2; W.7): a move of sealed files into the quarantine, or back to the image store, is
 * alerted once it has been due this long, and then daily (quarantine_due), as alert_steps() judges it: F's daily
 * threshold, make_interval(days => 1), which a database test holds to this number. The words that state it print it from

export const QUARANTINE_RULES = {

} as const;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the contact point

/** The two folders the watcher reads: the inbox, and the folder the mail host files junk in. */

export type ContactFolder = (typeof CONTACT_FOLDERS)[number];

/** What a message at the contact point turned out to be; `order` is set only by opening an order from it. */

/** The eight words of notify_state.error: why the watcher's last round failed. */
export const NOTIFY_ERRORS = ["imap_connect", "imap_timeout", "imap_tls", "imap_login", "imap_folder", "imap_protocol", "push_connect", "push_refused"] as const;

export const CONTACT_PAGE_SIZE = 50;

const Instant = z.iso.datetime();

/** One message at the contact point, as the console reads it: no sender, no subject and no content exist to show. */
export const ContactMessage = z.strictObject({
  id: z.uuid(),
  folder: z.enum(CONTACT_FOLDERS),
  receivedAt: Instant,
  seenAt: Instant,
  stale: z.boolean(),
  disposition: z.enum(CONTACT_DISPOSITIONS).nullable(),
  handledAt: Instant.nullable(),
  /** The staff handle of whoever closed it, or null. */
  handledBy: z.string().nullable(),
  /** The orders opened from it. */
  orders: z.array(z.uuid()),
});
export type ContactMessage = z.infer<typeof ContactMessage>;

/** GET /api/staff/contact: the messages newest first by receivedAt, a page at a time. */
export const ContactPage = z.strictObject({
  items: z.array(ContactMessage).max(CONTACT_PAGE_SIZE),
  nextCursor: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type ContactPage = z.infer<typeof ContactPage>;

/** The list's query: after the cursor the API handed out, and only the messages without a disposition with open=1. */
export const ContactQuery = z.strictObject({
  cursor: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional(),
  open: z.literal("1").optional(),
});
export type ContactQuery = z.infer<typeof ContactQuery>;

/** POST /api/staff/contact/:message/close. */
export const ContactCloseRequest = z.strictObject({ disposition: z.enum(CONTACT_CLOSE_DISPOSITIONS) });
export type ContactCloseRequest = z.infer<typeof ContactCloseRequest>;

/** The channel's state on the console's home: up, down, the mailbox unreadable, or switched off on this server. */
export const ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES = ["ok", "down", "mailbox", "off"] as const;
export type AlertChannelState = (typeof ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the alerts

/**
 * The closed list of alerts, the CHECK of alert_outbox.kind written from it: 3f's kinds, then 3c's and 3e's six, whose
 * mails stay their own and which gain a push, then 3d's.
 */
export const ALERT_KIND_LIST = [
  "contact_mail",
  "contact_mail_escalated",
  "order_due",
  "order_opened",
  "order_corrected",
  "order_effected",
  "order_reinstated",
  "order_unverified",
  "hold_ending",
  "report_owed",
  "handover_undestroyed",
  "copy_overdue",
  "copy_taken",
  "alert_channel_down",
  "mailbox_unreachable",
  "alert_test",
  "moderation_urgent",
  "moderation_waiting",
  "moderation_burst",
  "moderation_reads",
  "moderation_reveal",
  "moderation_csam_lifted",
  // 3d (design, section 10.1): its kinds, each a sentence to every staff account. Task 1: a move of sealed files that is
  // due (alert_steps(), daily) and files the quarantine's record says are lost (staff.js quarantine-record).
  "quarantine_due",
  "quarantine_lost",
  // Task 2: a released file still recorded in the quarantine (alert_steps(), daily), and an admin's release of sealed
  // images (after the release's commit, to every staff account, the admin who released included).
  "release_undestroyed",
  "seal_released",
  // Task 3: the outbox's job gave up on purges at the edge (its own row, under F's daily rule).
  "edge_purge_failed",
  // Task 5: the transparency job published a day's value without an outside timestamp, or found the day before without
  // a published value (each its own row, under F's daily rule).
  "head_unwitnessed",
  "head_missed",
  // Task 6: an author asked for a person about a program's measure (staffAlert after the objection's commit, at most once
  // in 15 minutes); a cap or a limit refused a program's measure (staffAlert after the step's commit, at most once an
  // hour); a request for a person waited longer than the published target (the sweep's own row, under F's daily rule).
  "automated_objection",
  "automation_capped",
  "automated_waiting",
  // Task 7: the comparison of uploads needs the operator (alert_steps(), daily, while a check stays unanswered; and at once
  // by the first upload of an hour that matched over the limit on refusals); and an admin ended a held upload's hold
  // without a report (staffAlert after the end's commit, to every staff account, the admin included, no throttle).
  "matcher_down",
  "hold_ended_unreported",
  // 3d review M13: a day's value whose keeper's mail never went out (the transparency job's own row in the next day's first
  // round, under F's daily rule, while HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL is set).
  "head_unmailed",
  // 3b Task 5 (the orchestrator's ruling on 3b design, section 8.1): imported images whose match does not act were left
  // out of their import and never published (staffAlert after the settling commit, at most once an hour an import).
  "import_image_flagged",
] as const;
export type AlertKind = (typeof ALERT_KIND_LIST)[number];

export type AlertLeg = "push" | "mail";
/** The ntfy topic of a push: the phone on call, or every staff phone. A mail goes to every staff account whatever the scope. */
export type AlertScope = "on_call" | "all";

/** One kind's entry: its priority and scope, its legs, who renders its mail, and the names of its facts. */
export interface AlertKindEntry {
  readonly priority: 3 | 5;
  readonly scope: AlertScope;
  readonly legs: readonly AlertLeg[];
  /**
   * `sentence`: the mail is the kind's own entry of ALERT_TEXTS, which the alert tick can mail again from the row's facts;
   * `own`: a mail of 3c or 3e that says more than the facts hold, which only staffAlert sends; null: pushed only.
   */
  readonly mail: "sentence" | "own" | null;
  /** The names of the row's facts: counts and times, at most six. */
  readonly facts: readonly string[];
}

const both: readonly AlertLeg[] = ["push", "mail"];
const sentenceKind = (priority: 3 | 5, scope: AlertScope, facts: readonly string[]): AlertKindEntry => ({ priority, scope, legs: both, mail: "sentence", facts });
const ownKind = (priority: 3 | 5, scope: AlertScope, facts: readonly string[]): AlertKindEntry => ({ priority, scope, legs: both, mail: "own", facts });

/**
 * Each kind's facts under the names the sentences print. `order_opened` carries `unknown` (1 for an order opened without
 * a time of receipt, else 0) beside its count and its deadline, so its sentence can tell "No deadline runs" from "Its
 * deadline is unknown"; `order_effected` carries `urgent` the same way.
 */
export const ALERT_KINDS: Record<AlertKind, AlertKindEntry> = {
  contact_mail: sentenceKind(5, "on_call", ["receivedAt", "dueAt"]),
  contact_mail_escalated: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["receivedAt", "dueAt"]),
  order_due: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["dueAt", "minutesLeft", "itemsOpen"]),
  order_opened: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["items", "dueAt", "unknown"]),
  order_corrected: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  order_effected: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["items", "at", "itemsOpen", "urgent"]),
  order_reinstated: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  order_unverified: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["count", "textsMissing", "holdsOpen", "oldestAt"]),
  hold_ending: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  report_owed: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  handover_undestroyed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  copy_overdue: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["hours"]),
  copy_taken: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "rows"]),
  alert_channel_down: { priority: 3, scope: "all", legs: ["mail"], mail: "sentence", facts: ["since"] },
  mailbox_unreachable: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["since"]),
  alert_test: { priority: 3, scope: "all", legs: ["push"], mail: null, facts: ["at"] },
  // 3d review L8: `count` is the lane's cases alone, `oldestAt` the oldest case's (absent when none waits), and
  // `heldUploads` the held uploads that wait, a fact of their own.
  moderation_urgent: ownKind(5, "on_call", ["count", "oldestAt", "heldUploads"]),
  moderation_waiting: ownKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  moderation_burst: ownKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  moderation_reads: ownKind(3, "all", ["limit"]),
  moderation_reveal: ownKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  moderation_csam_lifted: ownKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  quarantine_due: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  quarantine_lost: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  release_undestroyed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  seal_released: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "posts", "uploads"]),
  edge_purge_failed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  head_unwitnessed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["day"]),
  head_missed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["day"]),
  automated_objection: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "count"]),
  // The limit met is one of four facts, each 1 when present (CAP_LIMITS): a row's facts are counts and instants only, so
  // the limit's word cannot be a fact of its own.
  automation_capped: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "count", "limitHour", "limitDay", "limitUnanswered", "limitWaiting"]),
  automated_waiting: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  matcher_down: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["since", "count", "refusalsCapped"]),
  // The time after which the upload is deleted is a time fact, so it ends in At (W.7's `until`).
  hold_ended_unreported: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "deletesAt"]),
  head_unmailed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["day"]),
  // 3b Task 5: when, and how many images of one import the settling round left out as flagged.
  import_image_flagged: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "count"]),
};

/** The kinds the watcher publishes: every kind with a push leg. */
export const PUSH_KINDS: readonly AlertKind[] = ALERT_KIND_LIST.filter((kind) => ALERT_KINDS[kind].legs.includes("push"));
/** The kinds whose mail is their push's sentence, which the alert tick mails from the row. */
export const SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS: readonly AlertKind[] = ALERT_KIND_LIST.filter((kind) => ALERT_KINDS[kind].mail === "sentence");

/** The facts of a row: counts, and instants as ISO strings in UTC. */
export type AlertFacts = Readonly<Record<string, number | string>>;

/**
 * A fact that is a day (3d Task 5's head alerts): the row holds the day's first instant, as it holds every time, and
 * renderAlert prints it as the day itself ("2026-10-16", rule 7 of the 3d design's section 18), never as a time of day.
 */
export const isDayFact = (name: string): boolean => name === "day";

/** A fact that is a time: `at`, `since`, a name that ends in At, or a day. Every other fact is a count. */
export const isTimeFact = (name: string): boolean => name === "at" || name === "since" || name.endsWith("At") || isDayFact(name);

/** What a part of a sentence is printed under: a fact present or missing, above zero, or equal to 1 or not. */
export interface AlertCondition {
  readonly fact: string;
  readonly is: "present" | "absent" | "positive" | "one" | "not_one";
}
/** A part of a sentence, printed when its condition holds; the parts printed are joined with a space. */
export interface AlertPart {
  readonly text: string;
  /** One condition, or several that must all hold. */
  readonly when?: AlertCondition | readonly AlertCondition[];
}
/** A kind's words: the title, the sentence in parts, and for a kind whose mail is its sentence the mail's line of what to do. */
export interface AlertText {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly sentence: readonly AlertPart[];
  readonly todo: string | null;
}

const NOT_LISTED = 'An order you find there is opened in the console under Orders, with "The message is not listed".';
const KEY_TOLD = "Every staff account gets this. If it was confirmed with your key and not by you, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.";
const one = (text: string): readonly AlertPart[] => [{ text }];
```
