  // 3d review M13: the day is printed as a date (isDayFact).
  head_unmailed: {
    title: "The keeper did not get a daily value",
    sentence: one("The audit log's value of {day} was published, and its mail to the keeper never went out."),
    todo: "The operator checks the mail relay and HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL (staff.js automation-status prints the last mail's outcome). The keeper copies that day's value from /transparency and notes that its mail did not come.",
  },
  // 3b Task 5 (3b design, section 8.1): counts and a time only, never an image, an id, an import or a handle. An importer
  // chose none of thousands of images one by one, so a match that does not act publishes nothing, unlike a native upload.
  import_image_flagged: {
    title: "Imported images matched known material",
    sentence: one("{count} images being imported matched known material at {at}, in a way no program may act on. They were left out of the import and are not published."),
    todo: "Nothing touches the account and the person is not told of the match. The match records stay, as for any upload never posted. If this repeats, tell the operator: the source's list or the way to it may be faulty.",
  },
};

/**
 * A placeholder in braces: a fact's name, or a member of ORDER_RULES, of QUARANTINE_RULES, (3d Task 3) of EDGE_WORDS or (3d
 * Task 6) of AUTOMATION_RULES.
 */
const PLACEHOLDER = /[{]([a-zA-Z]+)[}]/g;

/** Every placeholder a kind's words name, each once. */
export function alertPlaceholders(kind: AlertKind): string[] {
  const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
  const words = [text.title, ...text.sentence.map((part) => part.text), text.todo ?? ""].join(" ");
  return [...new Set([...words.matchAll(PLACEHOLDER)].map((found) => found[1]!))];
}

/** The form of a time in a row's facts: an instant in UTC with up to six decimals of a second. */
export const ALERT_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}([.][0-9]{1,6})?Z$/;

const two = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");

/** An alert's time (rule 5 of section 18): "14:05 UTC", with the day before it when it is not the day of `now` in UTC. */
export function alertTime(iso: string, now: Date): string {
  const at = new Date(iso);
  const clock = `${two(at.getUTCHours())}:${two(at.getUTCMinutes())} UTC`;
  const day = `${at.getUTCFullYear()}-${two(at.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${two(at.getUTCDate())}`;
  const today = `${now.getUTCFullYear()}-${two(now.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${two(now.getUTCDate())}`;
  return day === today ? clock : `${day} ${clock}`;
}

/** Whether a part's condition, or every one of its conditions, holds for the facts. */
function holds(when: AlertPart["when"], facts: AlertFacts): boolean {
  if (when === undefined) return true;
  if (Array.isArray(when)) return when.every((condition: AlertCondition) => holds(condition, facts));
  const condition = when as AlertCondition;
  const value = facts[condition.fact];
  switch (condition.is) {
    case "present":
      return value !== undefined;
    case "absent":
      return value === undefined;
    case "positive":
      return typeof value === "number" && value > 0;
    case "one":
      return value === 1;
    case "not_one":
      return value !== 1;
  }
}

/** The facts held to the kind's names and kinds: a time where the name is a time's, a whole number elsewhere. */
function checkFacts(kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts): void {
  const names = ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts;
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(facts)) {
    if (!names.includes(name)) throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: the fact ${name} is not one of its facts`);
    if (isTimeFact(name) ? typeof value !== "string" || !ALERT_TIME.test(value) : typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
      throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: the fact ${name} is not ${isTimeFact(name) ? "a time" : "a count"}`);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * A kind's title, sentence and line of what to do, filled from the facts, ORDER_RULES, QUARANTINE_RULES and EDGE_WORDS. A time
 * prints as alertTime does at `now`, and a day as the date of its instant in UTC. A placeholder with nothing to fill it, a
 * fact of another kind and a fact of the wrong form throw: an alert never goes out with a hole or with anything but
 * counts and times in it.
 */
export function renderAlert(kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts, now: Date): { title: string; sentence: string; todo: string | null } {
  checkFacts(kind, facts);
  const rules = { ...ORDER_RULES, ...QUARANTINE_RULES, ...EDGE_WORDS, ...AUTOMATION_RULES } as Record<string, number | null>;
  const fill = (text: string) =>
    text.replace(PLACEHOLDER, (_match, name: string) => {
      const value = facts[name];
      if (value !== undefined) return typeof value === "string" ? (isDayFact(name) ? value.slice(0, 10) : alertTime(value, now)) : String(value);
      const rule = Object.hasOwn(rules, name) ? rules[name] : undefined;
      if (typeof rule === "number") return String(rule);
      throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: nothing fills {${name}}`);
    });
  const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
  return {
    title: fill(text.title),
    sentence: text.sentence
      .filter((part) => holds(part.when, facts))
      .map((part) => fill(part.text))
      .join(" "),
    todo: text.todo === null ? null : fill(text.todo),
  };
}

 */
export const REPORT_HOLD_RELEASES = ["sent", "declined", "expired"] as const;

 * W.8's sentence of what korbat does not hold, and of what it holds and has not produced, by version: a notification's
 * record stores the version that went with it (`not_kept_version`), so a changed sentence is a new version.
 */
export const RECORDS_NOT_HELD = {
  1: "korbat holds no name, postal address, date of birth, phone number or IP address of this account. It holds IP addresses, and a phone number the account verified, only as keyed hashes that identify nobody outside korbat; a device's hash is deleted 30 days after the device was last seen. korbat also holds, and has not produced here, the times and device types of the account's sign-ins.",
} as const;
export const RECORDS_NOT_HELD_VERSION = 1;

/**
 * The digest that a later step of a notification record (its answer, an event) and every step of a production hold in
 * their audit row in place of the facts (10.5): the SHA-256, in hex, of the record's row at that step in the canonical
 * JSON (canonical.ts), as the database printed it. The chain proves the record existed and was not changed afterwards,
 * and `staff.js records --verify` recomputes it from the row, without the audit log ever naming the person.
 */
export async function recordDigestOf(row: unknown): Promise<string> {
  return hex(await sha256(sortedJson(row)));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the requests (10.2, 10.3)

/** A uuid in the lower case PostgreSQL writes: the one spelling a hashed param may take. */
const LowerUuid = z.uuid().regex(/^[0-9a-f-]+$/, { message: "a uuid in lower case" });

/** Whether a text holds a control character: C0, DEL or C1. */
const hasControl = (text: string) =>
  [...text].some((char) => {
    const code = char.codePointAt(0)!;
    return code < 32 || (code >= 127 && code < 160);
  });
/** Whether a string is whole text, with no half of a surrogate pair. */
const isWellFormed = (text: string) => (text as string & { isWellFormed(): boolean }).isWellFormed();

/**
 * One line typed from an order's document: an authority's name, a reference, a link. Stored as written or refused: well
 * formed, no control character, none of the invisible direction and spacing characters, some text, at most `max`
 * characters as PostgreSQL counts them. It is an outsider's text, and the console draws it as such.
 */
const orderLine = (max: number) =>
  z
    .string()
    // A character outside the basic plane is two UTF-16 units, so this bound never refuses what the count below accepts.
    .max(2 * max)
    .refine(isWellFormed, { message: "half of a surrogate pair is not text" })
    .refine((text) => !hasControl(text), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
    .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
    .refine((text) => text.trim().length > 0, { message: "some text is needed" })
    .refine((text) => Array.from(text).length <= max, { message: `at most ${max} characters` });
export const OrderAuthority = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.name);
export const OrderReference = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.name);
export const OrderLinkText = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.link);

const distinct = (values: readonly string[]) => new Set(values).size === values.length;
const orderLinks = (min: number) => z.array(OrderLinkText).min(min).max(ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction).refine(distinct, { message: "a link is named once" });

/**
 * POST /api/staff/orders (7.4). sectionC is required and has no default: the form's third choice, "I cannot tell", is
 * sent as true. A named message comes with the channel mailbox, which the database forces too. The withholding is true
 * for a removal order and whenever Section C is set, so no request can hold a notice on a post its author sees; an order
 * to provide information names no post, so it does not withhold unless Section C forces it. It takes no link; the other
 * two kinds take one to itemsPerAction.
 */
export const OrderOpenRequest = z
  .strictObject({
    messageId: z.uuid().nullable(),
    channel: z.enum(ORDER_CHANNELS),
    kind: z.enum(ORDER_KINDS),
    memberState: MemberStateCode,
    authority: OrderAuthority,
    reference: OrderReference,
    links: orderLinks(0),
    sectionC: z.boolean(),
    emergency: z.boolean(),
    withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean(),
  })
  .superRefine((request, ctx) => {
    if (request.messageId !== null && request.channel !== "mailbox") ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["channel"], message: "an order opened from a message arrived in the mailbox" });
    if ((request.kind === "tco_removal" || request.sectionC) && !request.withholdFromAuthor) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "a removal order, and an order whose author must not be told, keeps the post from its author" });
    }
    if (request.kind === "dsa_art10" && !request.sectionC && request.withholdFromAuthor) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "an order to provide information names no post to withhold" });
    }
    if (request.kind === "dsa_art10" ? request.links.length > 0 : request.links.length === 0) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["links"], message: "an order to provide information takes no link; the other kinds take at least one" });
    }
  });
export type OrderOpenRequest = z.infer<typeof OrderOpenRequest>;

/** POST /api/staff/orders/:order/items: one to itemsPerAction more links, up to ORDER_ITEMS_MAX in all. */
export const OrderItemsRequest = z.strictObject({ links: orderLinks(1) });
export type OrderItemsRequest = z.infer<typeof OrderItemsRequest>;

/**
 * What a correction changes (7.4): only the members to change, at least one. crossBorder is the API's, set with
 * memberState. closeItems closes open items, each with one reason, no item twice. Section C set never comes with the
 * withholding unset.
 */
export const OrderCorrectFacts = z
  .strictObject({
    kind: z.enum(ORDER_KINDS).optional(),
    memberState: MemberStateCode.optional(),
    authority: OrderAuthority.optional(),
    reference: OrderReference.optional(),
    channel: z.enum(ORDER_CHANNELS).optional(),
    sectionC: z.boolean().optional(),
    emergency: z.boolean().optional(),
    withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean().optional(),
    closeItems: z
      .array(z.strictObject({ itemId: LowerUuid, reason: z.enum(ORDER_ITEM_CLOSE_REASONS) }))
      .min(1)
      .max(ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction)
      .refine((items) => distinct(items.map((item) => item.itemId)), { message: "an item is closed once" })
      .optional(),
  })
  .refine((facts) => Object.keys(facts).length > 0, { message: "a correction changes something" })
  .refine((facts) => !(facts.sectionC === true && facts.withholdFromAuthor === false), { message: "an order whose author must not be told keeps the post from its author", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"] });
export type OrderCorrectFacts = z.infer<typeof OrderCorrectFacts>;

/** The step-up params of order_corrected, asked only under the rule admin: the request's facts (10.3). */
export const OrderCorrectedParams = z.strictObject({ facts: OrderCorrectFacts });
export type OrderCorrectedParams = z.infer<typeof OrderCorrectedParams>;

/** Every ground a console event takes: an Annex III's and a closing's, each once. A param is never a free string. */
const CONSOLE_EVENT_GROUNDS = [...ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ...ORDER_CLOSE_GROUNDS] as const;

/**
 * The step-up params of order_event_recorded (10.3): the kind, its ground (one of its kind's list, or null for a kind
 * without one) and the message it names, which a clarification and an extension need, a cease may have and nothing else
 * takes.
 */
export const OrderEventRecordedParams = z
  .strictObject({ kind: z.enum(ORDER_CONSOLE_EVENTS), ground: z.enum(CONSOLE_EVENT_GROUNDS).nullable(), messageId: LowerUuid.nullable() })
  .superRefine((params, ctx) => {
    const grounds = orderEventGrounds(params.kind);
    if (grounds === null ? params.ground !== null : params.ground === null || !grounds.includes(params.ground)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["ground"], message: grounds === null ? "this event has no ground" : "a ground of this event's list" });
    }
    const needs = params.kind === "clarification_received" || params.kind === "hold_extended";
    const may = needs || params.kind === "grounds_ceased";
    if ((needs && params.messageId === null) || (!may && params.messageId !== null)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["messageId"], message: needs ? "this event names the message it came in" : "this event names no message" });
    }
  });
export type OrderEventRecordedParams = z.infer<typeof OrderEventRecordedParams>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the answers (10.2)

const At = z.iso.datetime();

/** A removal order's clock: one row of legal_order_clock, with the newest Annex III's time and ground while it is stopped. */
export const OrderClock = z.strictObject({
  clockStart: At.nullable(),
  stopped: z.boolean(),
  stoppedAt: At.nullable(),
  stopGround: z.enum(ANNEX3_GROUNDS).nullable(),
  deadlineAt: At.nullable(),
  targetAt: At.nullable(),
  itemsOpen: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  firstEffectAt: At.nullable(),
  lastEffectAt: At.nullable(),
  withinHour: z.boolean().nullable(),
});
export type OrderClock = z.infer<typeof OrderClock>;

/** One order on the list: its facts as typed, its clock (null for a DSA order), its state and its counts. */
export const OrderSummary = z.strictObject({
  id: z.uuid(),
  kind: z.enum(ORDER_KINDS),
  memberState: MemberStateCode,
  authority: z.string(),
  reference: z.string(),
  openedAt: At,
  state: z.enum(ORDER_STATES),
  clock: OrderClock.nullable(),
  /** A DSA order's deadline as its text states it, or null. */
  dueAt: At.nullable(),
  closedAt: At.nullable(),
  closeGround: z.enum(ORDER_CLOSE_GROUNDS).nullable(),
  items: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  itemsInForce: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  verified: z.boolean(),
  noticesHeld: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
});
export type OrderSummary = z.infer<typeof OrderSummary>;

/** GET /api/staff/orders: the orders that are not closed, the nearest deadline first, and those closed in the last 30 days. */
export const OrdersPage = z.strictObject({ open: z.array(OrderSummary), closed: z.array(OrderSummary) });
export type OrdersPage = z.infer<typeof OrdersPage>;

/** The stored states of a post, as an order's item reads them live. */
export const ORDER_ITEM_POST_STATES = ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "deleted_by_author", "disabled"] as const;

/** One item of an order: its link as named, what it resolved to (read live), and what became of it. */
export const OrderItemView = z.strictObject({
  id: z.uuid(),
  position: z.number().int().min(1).max(ORDER_ITEMS_MAX),
  link: z.string(),
  linkKind: z.enum(ORDER_LINK_KINDS),
  addedAt: At,
  /** The order is not verified, or the item was added after its verification. */
  unverified: z.boolean(),
  postId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  /** Null when the link named no post; the preview only while the post is public, and never an image. */
  post: z
    .strictObject({
      authorHandle: z.string().nullable(),
      state: z.enum(ORDER_ITEM_POST_STATES),
      images: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
      preview: z.string().nullable(),
      createdAt: At,
      deletedOn: z.iso.date().nullable(),
    })
    .nullable(),
  decisionId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  caseId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  inForce: z.boolean(),
  disabledAt: At.nullable(),
  noEffect: z.enum(["deleted", "already"]).nullable(),
  preserveUntil: At.nullable(),
  preserveEndedAt: At.nullable(),
  /**
   * Task 4 (sections 6.4 and 8.5, [item.erased]): when the preservation's end erased the post's content, the same instant
   * as preserveEndedAt; null while nothing was erased, and when the preservation ended without an erasure (a
   * reinstatement, a correction to another kind, or a measure no longer in force).
   */
  erasedAt: At.nullable(),
  reinstatedAt: At.nullable(),
  reinstatedGround: z.enum(ORDER_GROUNDS).nullable(),
  closedAt: At.nullable(),
  closedReason: z.enum(ORDER_ITEM_CLOSE_REASONS).nullable(),
  /** True when an open restore gap names the item (Task 6 builds the gaps); false until then. */
  gap: z.boolean(),
  /**
   * 3d Task 3 (design, sections 7.4 and 8.4): for an item that was disabled, the newest outbox row of each image of its
   * post that stopped being public, as a case carries them (CaseView.purges); empty for an item never disabled.
   */
  purges: z.array(EdgePurgeView),
});
export type OrderItemView = z.infer<typeof OrderItemView>;

/** One event of an order: who wrote it as a staff handle, or null for the command line and the database. */
export const OrderEventView = z.strictObject({
  id: z.uuid(),
  kind: z.enum(ORDER_EVENT_KINDS),
  ground: z.string().nullable(),
  at: At,
  effectiveAt: At.nullable(),
  itemId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  by: z.string().nullable(),
  via: z.enum(ORDER_EVENT_VIA),
});
export type OrderEventView = z.infer<typeof OrderEventView>;

/** What the command line still owes an order (7.5), and until when korbat may ask for a scrutiny. */
export const OrderOwed = z.strictObject({
  received: z.boolean(),
  verification: z.boolean(),
  issuedAt: z.boolean(),
  texts: z.boolean(),
  document: z.boolean(),
  holdUntil: z.boolean(),
  tellPerson: z.boolean(),
  scrutinyUntil: At.nullable(),
});
export type OrderOwed = z.infer<typeof OrderOwed>;

/** An order's hold, for an order with Section C: its end (null while a DSA order's has none recorded) and what became of it. */
export const OrderHold = z.strictObject({
  until: At.nullable(),
  basis: z.enum(HOLD_BASES),
  open: z.boolean(),
  extended: z.boolean(),
  endedAt: At.nullable(),
  endReason: z.enum(HOLD_END_REASONS).nullable(),
  releasedAt: At.nullable(),
  noticesHeld: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
});
export type OrderHold = z.infer<typeof OrderHold>;

/**
 * GET /api/staff/orders/:order: the summary with its items as a list, the row's facts, the events oldest first, what the
 * command line owes, the hold, and the console's aids (the database decides). No text of reasons, redress, scope,
 * verified_how or hold_basis: those are the command line's, and the author's notice is where the first three are read.
 */
export const OrderView = OrderSummary.extend({
  channel: z.enum(ORDER_CHANNELS),
  messageId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  receivedAt: At.nullable(),
  sentAt: At.nullable(),
  issuedAt: At.nullable(),
  sectionC: z.boolean(),
  emergency: z.boolean(),
  crossBorder: z.boolean(),
  withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean(),
  preserve: z.boolean(),
  openedBy: z.string().nullable(),
  openedVia: z.enum(["console", "cli"]),
  importedAt: At.nullable(),
  tellPerson: z.strictObject({ rule: z.enum(TELL_PERSON_RULES), at: At.nullable() }).nullable(),
  items: z.array(OrderItemView).max(ORDER_ITEMS_MAX),
  events: z.array(OrderEventView),
  owed: OrderOwed,
  hold: OrderHold.nullable(),
  mayClose: z.boolean(),
  mayEvents: z.array(z.enum(ORDER_CONSOLE_EVENTS)),
  mayCorrect: z.enum(ORDER_CORRECTION_RULES).nullable(),
});
export type OrderView = z.infer<typeof OrderView>;

/** The one refusal of 3f that carries a member: order_exists names the order that stands, so the console links to it. */
export const OrderExistsDetails = z.strictObject({ orderId: z.uuid() });
export type OrderExistsDetails = z.infer<typeof OrderExistsDetails>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- giving effect (Task 3: 7.6, 7.9, 10.1, 10.3, 10.4)

/**
 * What an order decision is by its order's kind (10.1), which decisions_record forces and OrderEffectedParams therefore
 * does not carry. The category of a DSA Article 9 order is a filler for a column that may not be null: korbat did not
 * assess the content, and nothing reads the column for such a decision. A dsa_art10 order is never given effect.
 */
export const ORDER_DECISION = {
  tco_removal: { category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY", keyword: "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT", preserves: true, effectBeforeVerified: true, holdBasis: "regulation" },
  dsa_art9: { category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE", keyword: null, preserves: false, effectBeforeVerified: false, holdBasis: "authority" },
} as const;

/** One item of an effect: an order's item and the post it names, both in lower case. */
const EffectItem = z.strictObject({ itemId: LowerUuid, postId: LowerUuid });

/**
 * The step-up params of order_effected (10.3): the order's facts as the console showed them, `urgent` and the items, 1 to
 * itemsPerAction, sorted by postId with no repeat of either id, so one action has one hash and its order is the lock
 * order. `authority` and `reference` are the one named exception to the rule that a param is never a free string: an
 * authority's name and its file number, bound as an order's lines are, which decision_holds compares with the order's
 * row at commit. `withholdFromAuthor` is true for a removal order and whenever Section C is set, and `urgent` is refused
 * for a removal order (the database refuses it on a verified order too).
 */
export const OrderEffectedParams = z
  .strictObject({
    kind: z.enum(["tco_removal", "dsa_art9"]),
    memberState: MemberStateCode,
    authority: OrderAuthority,
    reference: OrderReference,
    sectionC: z.boolean(),
    emergency: z.boolean(),
    withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean(),
    urgent: z.boolean(),
    items: z.array(EffectItem).min(1).max(ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction),
  })
  .superRefine((params, ctx) => {
    if ((params.kind === "tco_removal" || params.sectionC) && !params.withholdFromAuthor) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "a removal order, and an order whose author must not be told, keeps the post from its author" });
    }
    if (params.kind === "tco_removal" && params.urgent) ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["urgent"], message: "a removal order is given effect without a check first: urgent means nothing for it" });
    const posts = params.items.map((item) => item.postId);
    if (posts.some((post, i) => i > 0 && posts[i - 1]! >= post)) ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["items"], message: "the items are sorted by post, without repeats" });
    if (!distinct(params.items.map((item) => item.itemId))) ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["items"], message: "an item is named once" });
  });
export type OrderEffectedParams = z.infer<typeof OrderEffectedParams>;

/**
 * The fixed reasons of a reinstatement (W.2's reinstated.<ground>), which the composer saves as the correction's reason
 * and which nobody edits: a free text beside an order could say what a non-disclosure decision forbids.
 */
export const ORDER_DRAFTS = {
  reinstate: {
    withdrawn: "The authority that issued the order withdrew it.",
    annulled: "A court annulled the order.",
    scrutiny:
      "The competent authority of korbat's own Member State scrutinised the order and decided that it infringes the Regulation or fundamental rights, so the order no longer has effect (Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784).",
    not_authentic: "The order was not authentic: it did not come from the authority it named. korbat disabled your post on a forged order, and regrets it.",
    wrong_item: "korbat made a mistake: the order did not name this post. korbat disabled it wrongly, and regrets it.",
  },
} as const satisfies { reinstate: Record<OrderGround, string> };

const Day = z.string().regex(/^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$/, "must be a UTC day");

/**
 * What an order's notice is rendered from (10.4, W.2), built by the API at every read from the decision's row, its item's
 * and the order's as they stand, so the notice grows without a new decision. `verified` says whether order-verify has
 * run (until then the lead says only that the order names that authority); `orderedOn` is the day of the order's own
 * time stamp (`orderedFrom` issued) or of its receipt (received), or null; `held` whether the notice was held, and
 * `informedAt` the one instant the author was told (the release, for a held one); `holdEndReason` a hold ended by hand.
 * `preserveUntil` is the preservation's end as it stands, and (3f's review, people6) `preserveFirstUntil` its end six months
 * and a day from the disabling it counts from, before any extension; the two differ only once the preservation was extended.
 */
export const OrderNoticeFacts = z.object({
  kind: z.enum(["tco_removal", "dsa_art9"]),
  memberState: MemberStateCode,
  authority: z.string(),
  reference: z.string(),
  verified: z.boolean(),
  orderedOn: Day.nullable(),
  orderedFrom: z.enum(["issued", "received"]).nullable(),
  crossBorder: z.boolean(),
  homeState: MemberStateCode.nullable(),
  withholdAuthor: z.boolean(),
  disabledAt: At,
  held: z.boolean(),
  informedAt: At.nullable(),
  holdEndReason: z.enum(HOLD_END_REASONS).nullable(),
  preserveUntil: At.nullable(),
  preserveFirstUntil: At.nullable(),
  preserveExtended: z.boolean(),
  preserveEndedOn: Day.nullable(),
  orderGround: z.enum(ORDER_GROUNDS).nullable(),
});
export type OrderNoticeFacts = z.infer<typeof OrderNoticeFacts>;

/** The authority's words as the command line recorded them, read fresh, and since when the author holds the newest (10.4). */
export const OrderTexts = z.object({
  reasons: z.string().nullable(),
  redress: z.string().nullable(),
  scope: z.string().nullable(),
  textsAt: At.nullable(),
  // 3f's review (people2): since when the author holds the reasons themselves: the newest record of the reasons, or the
  // telling when that is later; null without reasons. A later record of the remedies or the scope moves textsAt only.
  reasonsAt: At.nullable(),
});
export type OrderTexts = z.infer<typeof OrderTexts>;

/** Home's [home.unverified] (10.2): the orders with a disabled item that are not verified, or whose disabled item was added after the check. */
export const OrdersUnverified = z.object({ total: z.number().int().nonnegative(), items: z.array(z.object({ orderId: z.uuid(), effectAt: At })).max(100) });
export type OrdersUnverified = z.infer<typeof OrdersUnverified>;

/**
 * Task 5 (sections 7.13 and 10.2): what `reports_owed()` answers and nothing more, for Home's [home.owed]: each owed
 * notification record's case, its kind (`sealed_images` for a seal's record, otherwise its first duty) and since when.
 * Who was reported to whom is the command line's alone.
 */
export const REPORT_OWED_KINDS = ["sealed_images", ...NOTIFICATION_DUTIES] as const;
export const ReportsOwed = z.object({
  total: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  items: z.array(z.object({ caseId: z.uuid(), kind: z.enum(REPORT_OWED_KINDS), since: At })).max(100),
});
export type ReportsOwed = z.infer<typeof ReportsOwed>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recovery (sections 6.6, 7.16, 7.17 and 10.1; Task 6)

/**
 * What an import after a restore found lost, by class, in the order in which a person takes it again (7.17, row 38): an
 * order's disablings, seals for good, seals taken while deciding, suspensions and terminations, other restrictions,
 * reversals, decisions without a measure (for reference), and the records the import could only note. The one list of
 * the CHECK on restore_gaps.class, of the import, of the console's After a restore screen and of the home screen's count.
 */
export const GAP_CLASSES = ["order_effect", "seal_final", "seal_interim", "release", "standing", "restriction", "reversal", "no_measure", "record"] as const;
export type GapClass = (typeof GAP_CLASSES)[number];
/** How a gap was closed: by a decision that took the measure again, by an admin as not needed, or as a record written again. */
export const GAP_DISPOSITIONS = ["reapplied", "not_needed", "imported"] as const;
export type GapDisposition = (typeof GAP_DISPOSITIONS)[number];
/**
 * The lost measures: while one of them is open, retention and the image sweep stay off (7.17 step 8). 3d's `release` (a
 * lost release, a lost leave or a lost withdrawal of one, which the operator replays or records again) is no measure, so
 * the list names its five classes rather than taking a slice of GAP_CLASSES, in which `release` stands fourth.
 */
export const GAP_MEASURE_CLASSES: readonly GapClass[] = ["order_effect", "seal_final", "seal_interim", "standing", "restriction"];
/**
 * The classes 1 to 4: while one of them is open, the app's site stays closed (RestoreView.mayOpen). 3d design, sections
 * 7.3 and 8.7: a `release` gap keeps it closed too, since until the replay the restored database counts as sealed and
 * kept what the record says was released. They are the first four of GAP_CLASSES, so the import's "gaps 1 to n" holds.
 */
export const GAP_SITE_CLASSES: readonly GapClass[] = GAP_CLASSES.slice(0, 4);

/** The most rows one download of the audit log's tail holds (7.16): a longer log is taken in several downloads. */
export const AUDIT_EXPORT_MAX = 50_000;

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { bigint, boolean, check, index, integer, pgEnum, pgTable, primaryKey, real, smallint, text, uniqueIndex, uuid, type AnyPgColumn } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { apiRole, bytea, fullAccess, ts } from "./helpers";
import { profiles } from "./identity";
import { importJobs, importSource } from "./imports";

/** 3f (design, section 6.2): `disabled`, a post an authority's order disables, which every reader answers as missing. */
export const postState = pgEnum("post_state", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "deleted_by_author", "disabled"]);

/**
 * What moderation derives for a post from the measures in force (3c design, section 6.1): the strongest of them.
 * posts.state mirrors it unless the author deleted the post, so post_state gains no value of 3c's. 3f adds `disabled`
 * to both (design, section 6.2), above `removed`: no row holds it before an order is given effect.
 */
export const moderationLevel = pgEnum("moderation_level", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "disabled"]);

/** An image's own moderation state, beside its post's. Only an image is ever sealed: shown to nobody, its author included. */
export const mediaModerationState = pgEnum("media_moderation_state", ["visible", "withheld", "removed", "sealed"]);

/** A counter kept exact by the application: updated in the same transaction as the action it counts. */
const counter = (name: string) => integer(name).notNull().default(0);

export const posts = pgTable(
  "posts",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    authorId: uuid("author_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    body: text("body").notNull(),
    replyToId: uuid("reply_to_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => posts.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
    quoteOfId: uuid("quote_of_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => posts.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
    state: postState("state").notNull().default("visible"),
    likeCount: counter("like_count"),
    repostCount: counter("repost_count"),
    /** Replies that are not deleted. */
    replyCount: counter("reply_count"),
    /** Quotes that are not deleted. */
    quoteCount: counter("quote_count"),
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    /** Set together with state = 'deleted_by_author'; the body is blanked at the same time. */
    deletedAt: ts("deleted_at"),
    /** Derived from the ledger of measures by a migrator-owned function, the only writer; the API role cannot update it. */
    moderationLevel: moderationLevel("moderation_level").notNull().default("visible"),
    /** Set, one way, when the R4 redaction erased the post's content; written only by a migrator-owned function. */
    erasedAt: ts("erased_at"),
    /**
     * Explore's resume rule (3e design, sections 6.1 and 6.4): when the post last left the level visible, when it last came
     * back, and the time its age and window are counted from after its hidden spans. Outside the API's column grants; a
     * later migration gives them their one writer, moderation_apply.
     */
    hiddenAt: ts("hidden_at"),
    restoredAt: ts("restored_at"),
    exploreFrom: ts("explore_from"),
    /**
     * 3b (design, section 6.2): an imported post's import, source, the date its archive gives it, whether it was cut to
     * 1,000 characters, and the key of section 5.4 (32 bytes) by which a later import of the account skips it. All five
     * are set or none is (a native post, or an imported one's tombstone); posts_import_guard (migration 0044) lets an
     * insert set them only for a publishing import of the author with the same source, and an update only clear them, all
     * at once, with the post's tombstone. No on delete clause on the job: its row cannot go while a post names it.
     */
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => importJobs.id),
    importSource: importSource("import_source"),
    originalCreatedAt: ts("original_created_at"),
    importShortened: boolean("import_shortened"),
    importKey: bytea("import_key"),
  },
  (t) => [
    index("posts_author_created_idx").on(t.authorId, t.createdAt),
    /** Explore's restored posts. */
    index("posts_explore_from_idx").on(t.exploreFrom).where(sql`explore_from is not null`),
    index("posts_created_id_idx").on(t.createdAt, t.id),
    /** A thread's replies in order, and every lookup by parent. */
    index("posts_reply_to_created_idx").on(t.replyToId, t.createdAt, t.id),
    /**
     * The public Latest timeline: visible top-level posts and quotes, newest first. 3b (6.2): imported posts are in no
     * feed, so the predicate leaves them out (migration 0045 drops the index and creates it again).
     */
    index("posts_latest_idx").on(t.createdAt, t.id).where(sql`reply_to_id is null and state = 'visible' and import_job_id is null`),
    index("posts_quote_of_idx").on(t.quoteOfId),
    /** 3b: a post is imported once per account while it exists (decision 24). */
    uniqueIndex("posts_import_key_idx").on(t.authorId, t.importKey).where(sql`import_key is not null`),
    /** 3b: an import's posts, for the undo, the foreign key's checks and the job's count. */
    index("posts_import_job_idx").on(t.importJobId, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null`),
    /** 3b (0045): the profile's Imported tab, its top-level imported posts by the archive's date. */
    index("posts_imported_idx").on(t.authorId, t.originalCreatedAt, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null and reply_to_id is null`),
    /**
     * 3b (0045): an author's native posts, for Following's own branch and the Posts and Replies tabs, so a followed
     * account's 50,000 imported posts are never scanned there.
     */
    index("posts_author_native_idx").on(t.authorId, t.createdAt, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is null`),
    check("posts_body_len", sql`char_length(${t.body}) <= 1000`),
    check("posts_counts_nonnegative", sql`${t.likeCount} >= 0 and ${t.repostCount} >= 0 and ${t.replyCount} >= 0 and ${t.quoteCount} >= 0`),
    check(
      "posts_import_columns",
      sql`(${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importSource} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.originalCreatedAt} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importShortened} is null) and (${t.importJobId} is null) = (${t.importKey} is null)`,
    ),
    fullAccess("posts_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * One Explore ranking (a "generation"), written by the refresh job (2c design, sections 6 and 7). The current ranking
 * is the highest generation; the job also keeps the one before it, so a reader paging through a ranking is not cut
 * off by the next round.
 */
export const exploreRuns = pgTable(
  "explore_runs",
  {
    /** Numbered by the database. One ranking every 5 minutes lasts 20,000 years in an integer. */
    generation: integer("generation").primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    /** The refresh time the round was given; the ranking is computed as of this time. */
    asOf: ts("as_of").notNull(),
    /** The version of the formula the round ranked with (EXPLORE_V2.version in @korbat/contracts; rankings from before 3e hold 1). */
    formula: smallint("formula").notNull(),
    /** Posts that passed the candidate predicate at as_of. */
    candidates: integer("candidates").notNull(),
    /** Posts the ranking holds; their positions run from 1 to this. */
    items: integer("items").notNull(),
    /** How long the round took. */
    tookMs: integer("took_ms").notNull(),
  },
  () => [fullAccess("explore_runs_api_all", apiRole)],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The posts of one Explore ranking, in order. No score or count is stored: nothing reads them after the insert, and
 * the position is the order. A row goes with its ranking, its post or its author.
 */
export const exploreItems = pgTable(
  "explore_items",
  {
    generation: integer("generation").notNull().references(() => exploreRuns.generation, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** 1 to the ranking's item count, without gaps. */
    position: integer("position").notNull(),
    postId: uuid("post_id").notNull().references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** The post's author, so an author's places in a ranking are counted without reading the posts. */
    authorId: uuid("author_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  },
  (t) => [
    primaryKey({ columns: [t.generation, t.position] }),
    /** A post has one place in a ranking. */
    uniqueIndex("explore_items_generation_post_idx").on(t.generation, t.postId),
    fullAccess("explore_items_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/** An upload is processing until the worker's result is in, then ready or failed for good. */
export const mediaStatus = pgEnum("media_status", ["processing", "ready", "failed"]);

/**
 * One uploaded image. The files live on the media-store volume under the row's id; no path is
 * stored. Only the API's media module reads or writes this table.
 */
export const postMedia = pgTable(
  "post_media",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    /** Who uploaded it. Only this account may attach it to a post. */
    ownerId: uuid("owner_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    status: mediaStatus("status").notNull().default("processing"),
    /** Why processing failed: one of the contracts' MediaFailure values. */
    error: text("error"),
    /** Set, together with the position, when the image is attached to a post. */
    postId: uuid("post_id").references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    position: integer("position"),
    /** Of the large size, after rotation. Set, together with the blurhash, when processing succeeds. */
    width: integer("width"),
    height: integer("height"),
    blurhash: text("blurhash"),
    altText: text("alt_text"),
    /** Filled by sub-project 3. Empty until then. */
    nsfwScore: real("nsfw_score"),
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    // The three columns below are forced to their defaults at insert and written only by migrator-owned functions; the
    // API role holds no UPDATE on them (migration 0015).
    /** Derived from the ledger of measures, as the post's level is. */
    moderationState: mediaModerationState("moderation_state").notNull().default("visible"),
    /** The latest end of the image's unreleased holds (media_holds): while it lies ahead, every delete skips the row. */
    holdUntil: ts("hold_until"),
    /** Set when an R4 removal of the image became final and its content was erased. */
    erasedAt: ts("erased_at"),
    /**
     * 3b (design, section 6.3): the image came from an import, which never changes; and the running import that owns the
     * upload, so the sweeper leaves it alone and the import cleans it up. post_media_import_insert (migration 0044) takes an
     * imported row only for a preparing import of its owner and a native one naming no import; the API role holds no
     * UPDATE of either. The import's row may go first: then its id is set null and the row stays imported, which
     * post_media_import_attach lets onto no post.
     */
    imported: boolean("imported").notNull().default(false),
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id").references((): AnyPgColumn => importJobs.id, { onDelete: "set null" }),
  },
  (t) => [
    uniqueIndex("post_media_post_position_idx").on(t.postId, t.position),
    index("post_media_owner_created_idx").on(t.ownerId, t.createdAt),
    index("post_media_status_created_idx").on(t.status, t.createdAt),
    check("post_media_ready_has_dims", sql`${t.status} <> 'ready' or (${t.width} is not null and ${t.height} is not null and ${t.blurhash} is not null)`),
    check("post_media_attached_is_complete", sql`${t.postId} is null or (${t.status} = 'ready' and ${t.position} between 0 and 3 and ${t.altText} is not null)`),
    check("post_media_alt_len", sql`char_length(${t.altText}) <= 1000`),
    check("post_media_import_link", sql`${t.importJobId} is null or ${t.imported}`),
    /**
     * 3b: an import's images by their job. The foreign key's set null when a job row goes, and the import's cleanup of its
     * unattached rows in id order (media.deleteImportLeftovers), would scan post_media without it.
     */
    index("post_media_import_job_idx").on(t.importJobId, t.id).where(sql`import_job_id is not null`),
    /**
     * 3b Task 5: the imports whose images are still on no post. import-drive asks it every round, for every import that
     * has ended, so that a stop's or a time limit's leftovers go (7.4); the index holds only rows on their way, never the
     * many attached ones, so the question costs nothing however many images were ever imported.
     */
    index("post_media_import_unattached_idx").on(t.importJobId).where(sql`import_job_id is not null and post_id is null`),
    fullAccess("post_media_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The edge's outbox (3d design, sections 2 row 11, 6.3 and 7.4; Task 3): one row each time an image stops being public,
 * which the job edge-purge drains to the purge adapter. No role inserts a row: the two definer triggers post_media_purge
 * and posts_purge write it in the transaction that hides the image, whoever the writer is, and the API's role holds no
 * INSERT, so no route can forget one and none can invent one. The insert trigger edge_purges_insert forces `created_at`
 * (clock_timestamp()) and `next_at` (now(): due at once). The API's job reads it, moves the four columns of a purge's
 * progress and (Task 8) deletes a row 30 days after it was done. No foreign key: an image's row may go, by a deletion or
 * the disposal, while its purge is still owed. The closed lists are the contracts' EDGE_PURGE_CAUSES and
 * EDGE_PURGE_OUTCOMES, written out here; a database test holds each migrated CHECK to its constant.
 */
export const edgePurges = pgTable(
  "edge_purges",
  {
    id: bigint("id", { mode: "number" }).primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    mediaId: uuid("media_id").notNull(),
    /** state, deleted or released. */
    cause: text("cause").notNull(),
    /** Forced: clock_timestamp(). */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull(),
    /** Forced at insert: now(). The job moves it back off after a failed purge. */
    nextAt: ts("next_at").notNull(),
    attempts: smallint("attempts").notNull().default(0),
    /** accepted, failed or off; set with done_at, once. */
    outcome: text("outcome"),
    doneAt: ts("done_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    check("edge_purges_cause", sql`${t.cause} in ('state', 'deleted', 'released')`),
    check("edge_purges_outcome", sql`${t.outcome} in ('accepted', 'failed', 'off')`),
    check("edge_purges_done", sql`(${t.outcome} is null) = (${t.doneAt} is null)`),
    check("edge_purges_attempts", sql`${t.attempts} >= 0`),
    /** The job's round: the rows still owed a purge, by when they are due. */
    index("edge_purges_due_idx").on(t.nextAt).where(sql`done_at is null`),
    /** The case's and the order's purge line: the newest row of an image. */
    index("edge_purges_media_idx").on(t.mediaId, t.id),
    fullAccess("edge_purges_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/** user -> user relation table (follows, blocks, mutes). */
function userPairTable(name: string, from: string, to: string) {
  return pgTable(
    name,
    {
      fromId: uuid(from).notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      toId: uuid(to).notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    },
    (t) => [
      primaryKey({ columns: [t.fromId, t.toId] }),
      /** Pages of either side, newest first, and every lookup by either side. */
      index(`${name}_to_created_idx`).on(t.toId, t.createdAt, t.fromId),
      index(`${name}_from_created_idx`).on(t.fromId, t.createdAt, t.toId),
      check(`${name}_not_self`, sql`${t.fromId} <> ${t.toId}`),
      fullAccess(`${name}_api_all`, apiRole),
    ],
  ).enableRLS();
}

/**
 * user -> post relation table (likes, reposts, bookmarks). `createdBrin` adds `<name>_created_brin`, a BRIN index on
 * created_at, for the tables whose recent rows the Explore refresh reads (2c design, section 6).
 */
function userPostTable(name: string, options: { createdBrin?: boolean } = {}) {
  return pgTable(
    name,
    {
      userId: uuid("user_id").notNull().references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      postId: uuid("post_id").notNull().references(() => posts.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
      createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    },
    (t) => [
      primaryKey({ columns: [t.userId, t.postId] }),
      index(`${name}_post_idx`).on(t.postId),
      /** Per-account lists (your likes, your bookmarks) and the reposts half of the Following timeline. */
      index(`${name}_user_created_idx`).on(t.userId, t.createdAt),
      // Rows arrive roughly in time order, so a BRIN index of a few kilobytes finds the refresh's window as fast as a
      // btree of many megabytes. Unlikes, blocks and purges let later rows fill old pages and erode that order slowly.
      ...(options.createdBrin ? [index(`${name}_created_brin`).using("brin", t.createdAt)] : []),
      fullAccess(`${name}_api_all`, apiRole),
    ],
  ).enableRLS();
}

export const follows = userPairTable("follows", "follower_id", "followee_id");
export const blocks = userPairTable("blocks", "blocker_id", "blocked_id");
export const mutes = userPairTable("mutes", "muter_id", "muted_id");
export const likes = userPostTable("likes", { createdBrin: true });
export const reposts = userPostTable("reposts", { createdBrin: true });
/** Bookmarks are private and never count towards Explore, so they need no index by time. */
export const bookmarks = userPostTable("bookmarks");

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { bigint, boolean, check, date, index, integer, jsonb, pgEnum, pgTable, primaryKey, smallint, text, uniqueIndex, uuid } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { apiRole, bytea, fullAccess, ts } from "./helpers";
import { profiles } from "./identity";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- import from other platforms (3b design, sections 6.1, 6.4 and 6.7; Task 2)
// The three tables of the migration imports. Only the API's imports module names them. The closed lists and numbers are
// the contracts' (packages/contracts/src/imports.ts: IMPORT_SOURCE_KINDS, ImportStatus, IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES,
// IMPORT_FAILURES, IMPORT_STOP_REASONS and IMPORT_RULES), written out here because this package does not depend on the
// contracts; apps/api/test/integration/import-schema.test.ts holds every migrated CHECK, enum and predicate equal to them.
// The migration's hand-written part adds the triggers that force an insert's columns, walk the states of section 4.1 and
// guard the deletes, and the API role's grants.

/** Where an archive came from. A later source is one more value (section 1.4). */
export const importSource = pgEnum("import_source", ["x", "mastodon", "bluesky"]);

/** The twelve states of section 4.1, in ImportStatus's order. The first five are active. */
export const importStatus = pgEnum("import_status", ["uploading", "scanning", "ready", "preparing", "publishing", "done", "stopped", "undoing", "undone", "failed", "cancelled", "expired"]);

/**
 * One import (6.1): an archive's upload, its scan, the person's choice and the publishing, as one row moving through the
 * twelve states. It holds the source, the state, the times, the choice and counts only: never a file name, a handle or a
 * text, but the first words of a post whose image was refused, shown to the person alone (decision 25). import_jobs_insert
 * forces every column but the id, the owner, the source and the size; import_jobs_guard lets each later column change
 * only by the move that names it. A post names its import (posts.import_job_id), so the row stays while one does.
 */
export const importJobs = pgTable(
  "import_jobs",
  {
    /** Made by the API (randomUUID): it names the import's folders on the two volumes. */
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey(),
    /** No on delete clause: no profile row is ever deleted. */
    ownerId: uuid("owner_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => profiles.id),
    source: importSource("source").notNull(),
    /** Forced to uploading at insert. */
    status: importStatus("status").notNull().default("uploading"),
    /** The archive's size as the person's app declared it: 1 byte to IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes. */
    declaredBytes: bigint("declared_bytes", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    /** Bytes stored so far; only grows, never past the declared size. */
    receivedBytes: bigint("received_bytes", { mode: "number" }).notNull().default(0),
    /** Forced to clock_timestamp() at insert. */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    /** Each set once, by the move that names it: into scanning, out of scanning, out of ready by a confirmation. */
    uploadedAt: ts("uploaded_at"),
    scannedAt: ts("scanned_at"),
    confirmedAt: ts("confirmed_at"),
    /** Set by the move into done, stopped, failed, cancelled or expired, and again by the move into undone. */
    endedAt: ts("ended_at"),
    /** IMPORT_FAILURES; set exactly when the state is failed. */
    failure: text("failure"),
    /** IMPORT_STOP_REASONS; set by the move into stopped, and kept through undoing and undone. */
    stopReason: text("stop_reason"),
    /** An admin's end of the whole import (8.7): when, and under which rule. Set together, once. */
    staffEndedAt: ts("staff_ended_at"),
    staffRuleId: text("staff_rule_id"),
    /** The archive's day and first words of the post whose image was refused (8.2). Set together, once. */
    refusedAtOriginal: date("refused_at_original"),
    refusedWords: text("refused_words"),
    /** The intake's numbers (ImportScanFacts); never a text. Set by the move into ready, and cut down by the move out of it. */
    scan: jsonb("scan"),
    /** ImportChoice, the person's statement and the seed come with the confirmation, together and once. */
    choice: jsonb("choice"),
    statedAt: ts("stated_at"),
    /** 32 random bytes from which the import's post and image ids are derived (6.5); cleared when the import ends. */
    seed: bytea("seed"),
    /** Lines of posts.jsonl handled, and images handed to the feeder; each only grows. */
    postCursor: integer("post_cursor").notNull().default(0),
    imageCursor: integer("image_cursor").notNull().default(0),
    /** Progress counts; each only grows. */
    postsPublished: integer("posts_published").notNull().default(0),
    imagesKept: integer("images_kept").notNull().default(0),
    imagesLeftOut: integer("images_left_out").notNull().default(0),
    postsRemoved: integer("posts_removed").notNull().default(0),
    /**
     * 3b Task 4 (the orchestrator's ruling; migration 0046): whether this import brings images, decided once at its
     * creation (IMPORT_IMAGES on, which the API allows only beside a matcher, decision 15) and written into job.json. The
     * API role inserts it and holds no UPDATE of it, so it never changes; the preview's media route reads it from here.
     */
    images: boolean("images").notNull().default(false),
    /**
     * 3b Task 5 (the orchestrator's ruling; migration 0047): the images the preparation left out, as counts by reason of
     * IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS (missing_file, unsupported, too_large, failed, flagged, not_checked), whose sum is always
     * images_left_out, so the result can say why. Forced to an empty object at insert; each count only grows.
     */
    imagesLeftOutBy: jsonb("images_left_out_by").notNull().default(sql`'{}'::jsonb`),
  },
  (t) => [
    // IMPORT_RULES.maxBytes.
    check("import_jobs_declared_bytes", sql`${t.declaredBytes} between 1 and 2147483648`),
    check("import_jobs_received_bytes", sql`${t.receivedBytes} between 0 and ${t.declaredBytes}`),
    // IMPORT_FAILURES.
    check(
      "import_jobs_failure",
      sql`${t.failure} in ('not_this_source', 'not_an_archive', 'tar_gz', 'partial_archive', 'encrypted', 'too_many_entries', 'too_large_uncompressed', 'bad_entry_name', 'unreadable', 'nothing_to_import', 'scan_timed_out', 'interrupted')`,
    ),
    // The state is compared as text, as 3b compares every enum (section 6).
    check("import_jobs_failed", sql`(${t.status}::text = 'failed') = (${t.failure} is not null)`),
    // IMPORT_STOP_REASONS.
    check("import_jobs_stop_reason", sql`${t.stopReason} in ('refused_image', 'by_author', 'by_staff', 'time_ran_out')`),
    // A stopped import has its reason; the reason stays through the undo, and no other state has one.
    check("import_jobs_stopped", sql`(${t.status}::text <> 'stopped' or ${t.stopReason} is not null) and (${t.stopReason} is null or ${t.status}::text in ('stopped', 'undoing', 'undone'))`),
    check("import_jobs_staff", sql`(${t.staffEndedAt} is null) = (${t.staffRuleId} is null)`),
    check("import_jobs_refused", sql`(${t.refusedAtOriginal} is null) = (${t.refusedWords} is null)`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.refusedWordsMax, in code points.
    check("import_jobs_refused_words", sql`char_length(${t.refusedWords}) <= 80`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.scanMaxBytes and choiceMaxBytes, as the bytes of the jsonb's text form.
    check("import_jobs_scan", sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.scan}) = 'object' and octet_length(${t.scan}::text) <= 262144`),
    check("import_jobs_choice", sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.choice}) = 'object' and octet_length(${t.choice}::text) <= 1024`),
    // The statement is never stored without the choice it confirmed, nor the choice without it.
    check("import_jobs_stated", sql`(${t.choice} is null) = (${t.statedAt} is null)`),
    // IMPORT_RULES.seedBytes.
    check("import_jobs_seed", sql`octet_length(${t.seed}) = 32`),
    // IMPORT_IMAGE_SKIPS: an object whose names are reasons of the list (the jsonb less those keys is empty), in at most
    // 1,024 bytes of its text form. That each count is a whole number that only grows, summing to images_left_out, is
    // import_jobs_guard's (0047).
    check(
      "import_jobs_left_out_by",
      sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.imagesLeftOutBy}) = 'object' and octet_length(${t.imagesLeftOutBy}::text) <= 1024 and (${t.imagesLeftOutBy} - array['video', 'sensitive', 'unsupported', 'too_large', 'missing_file', 'bluesky_no_files', 'images_off', 'not_chosen', 'no_description', 'over_image_cap', 'failed', 'not_checked', 'flagged']) = '{}'::jsonb`,
    ),
    check(
      "import_jobs_counts",
      sql`${t.postCursor} >= 0 and ${t.imageCursor} >= 0 and ${t.postsPublished} >= 0 and ${t.imagesKept} >= 0 and ${t.imagesLeftOut} >= 0 and ${t.postsRemoved} >= 0`,
    ),
    /**
     * One active import an account (4.1): the five states of IMPORT_ACTIVE_STATES. The enum's labels are literals here, not
     * text: an index predicate takes only immutable expressions, and the cast of an enum to text is not one. The type is
     * created in the same migration, so its labels are usable at once.
     */
    uniqueIndex("import_jobs_one_active").on(t.ownerId).where(sql`status in ('uploading', 'scanning', 'ready', 'preparing', 'publishing')`),
    /** import-drive's rounds, by state and age. */
    index("import_jobs_status_idx").on(t.status, t.createdAt),
    /** The account's list of its imports, and the purge's. */
    index("import_jobs_owner_idx").on(t.ownerId, t.createdAt),
    fullAccess("import_jobs_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The person's choices post by post (4.4): a line of posts.jsonl left out, and a description for each of its images the
 * source gave none, by position. Written only while the import is ready (import_picks_guard); deleted when the import
 * ends, and with the import's row in any case.
 */
export const importPicks = pgTable(
  "import_picks",
  {
    importJobId: uuid("import_job_id")
      .notNull()
      .references(() => importJobs.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    /** The line's ref, its place in posts.jsonl. */
    ref: integer("ref").notNull(),
    leftOut: boolean("left_out").notNull().default(false),
    /** An array of at most MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST AltText or null, or null. */
    alts: jsonb("alts"),
    /**
     * 3b Task 4 (the orchestrator's ruling; migration 0046): the picked line's month (YYYY-MM), its marks (IMPORT_MARKS as
     * bits) and how many of its images its source described, copied from posts.jsonl when the pick is first written. The
     * picks' counts of ImportView and ImportPickView are summed from these rows alone, so reading an import opens no work
     * file but the samples. The API role inserts them and holds no UPDATE of them: a line's facts never change.
     */
    month: text("month").notNull(),
    marks: smallint("marks").notNull(),
    described: smallint("described").notNull().default(0),
  },
  (t) => [
    primaryKey({ columns: [t.importJobId, t.ref] }),
    check("import_picks_month", sql`${t.month} ~ '^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$'`),
    // IMPORT_MARKS: four bits.
    check("import_picks_marks", sql`${t.marks} between 0 and 15`),
    // MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST.
    check("import_picks_described", sql`${t.described} between 0 and 4`),
    // At most four descriptions (MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST) in IMPORT_RULES.altsMaxBytes, as the bytes of the jsonb's text form:
    // four AltText of 1,000 code points take up to 16,016 (Task 1's amendment). A CASE, so the length is read only of an array.
    check(
      "import_picks_alts",
      sql`case jsonb_typeof(${t.alts}) when 'array' then jsonb_array_length(${t.alts}) <= 4 and octet_length(${t.alts}::text) <= 16384 else ${t.alts} is null end`,
    ),
    fullAccess("import_picks_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * Each importing account's random key of section 5.4, under which the importer hashes every source post's id, so a later
 * import skips what an earlier one published (decision 24) and two accounts' imports are never linked. Inserted at the
 * account's first import; never updated (the API role holds no UPDATE); deleted only once the profile is (the purge).
 */
export const importKeys = pgTable(
  "import_keys",
  {
    /** No on delete clause: no profile row is ever deleted. */
    ownerId: uuid("owner_id")
      .primaryKey()
      .references(() => profiles.id),
    key: bytea("key").notNull(),
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
  },
  (t) => [
    // IMPORT_RULES.keyBytes.
    check("import_keys_key", sql`octet_length(${t.key}) = 32`),
    fullAccess("import_keys_api_all", apiRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { bigint, bigserial, boolean, check, index, integer, jsonb, pgPolicy, pgTable, smallint, text, unique, uniqueIndex, uuid } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { apiRole, fullAccess, notifyRole, ts } from "./helpers";
import { profiles } from "./identity";

/**
 * Append-only, and since 3a a hash chain (3a design, section 6): the record of every staff action. UPDATE, DELETE and
 * TRUNCATE are revoked from the API role at the grant level (migration 0001). The trigger audit_chain, which migration 0012
 * installs and the migrator owns, sets id, created_at and the four chain columns of every inserted row, whatever the insert
 * supplied, under a lock on audit_head that lasts until the inserting transaction ends: an audit row is always the last
 * statement of its transaction.
 */
export const auditLog = pgTable(
  "audit_log",
  {
    id: bigserial("id", { mode: "number" }).primaryKey(),
    actorId: uuid("actor_id").notNull(),
    action: text("action").notNull(),
    targetType: text("target_type"),
    targetId: text("target_id"),
    metadata: jsonb("metadata").notNull().default(sql`'{}'::jsonb`),
    requestId: text("request_id"),
    /** When the row joined the chain, in milliseconds: the trigger sets it. */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull().defaultNow(),
    /** The handle of the staff session the action came from. */
    staffSession: uuid("staff_session"),
    /** The staff key: the one a step-up confirmed with, or the key a key's row is about. */
    keyId: uuid("key_id"),
    /** The lower-case hex sha256 of the confirmed action's sorted JSON, when a step-up confirmed it. */
    actionHash: text("action_hash"),
    /** The step-up assertion (authenticatorData, clientDataJSON, signature), base64url exactly as the browser sent them. */
    stepUp: jsonb("step_up").$type<{ authenticatorData: string; clientDataJSON: string; signature: string }>(),
    // The chain. The defaults are placeholders the trigger always overwrites: they keep drizzle's insert type from asking
    // for these columns and let migration 0012 add them over existing rows.
    /** The canonical text's version the row was hashed with. */
    chainVersion: smallint("chain_version").notNull().default(0),
    /** The row's place: the order in which inserts took the head's lock, from 1, with no gap. */
    chainSeq: bigint("chain_seq", { mode: "number" }).notNull().default(0),
    /** The hash of the row before it; 64 zeros for the first. */
    prevHash: text("prev_hash").notNull().default(""),
    /** sha256 hex of prev_hash followed by the row's canonical text. */
    hash: text("hash").notNull().default(""),
  },
  (t) => [
    // Serves the viewer and audit-verify. Migration 0012 creates it after the back-fill, which the placeholders would fail.
    uniqueIndex("audit_log_chain_seq_idx").on(t.chainSeq),
    // A step-up leaves its action's hash and its assertion together, with the key that made it.
    check("audit_log_step_up_complete", sql`(${t.actionHash} is null) = (${t.stepUp} is null) and (${t.actionHash} is null or ${t.keyId} is not null)`),
    pgPolicy("audit_log_api_insert", { for: "insert", to: apiRole, withCheck: sql`true` }),
    pgPolicy("audit_log_api_select", { for: "select", to: apiRole, using: sql`true` }),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * The newest row of the audit chain: its place and hash, or (1, 0, 64 zeros) for an empty log. One row, which only the
 * trigger moves. The API role may read it (audit-head and audit-verify check that it names the newest row) but neither write
 * nor lock it: migration 0012 revokes every other privilege, and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE needs UPDATE.
 */
export const auditHead = pgTable(
  "audit_head",
  {
    id: smallint("id").primaryKey(),
    seq: bigint("seq", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    hash: text("hash").notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [check("audit_head_single_row", sql`${t.id} = 1`), pgPolicy("audit_head_api_select", { for: "select", to: apiRole, using: sql`true` })],
).enableRLS();

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the contact point and the alert channel (3f design, section 6.1)

/**
 * One message at the authorities' contact point, one row a message, which the watcher (role korbat_notify) inserts with
 * four columns: the folder, the two numbers IMAP gives it and the mail host's time of final delivery. It holds no sender,
 * no subject and no content. The triggers of the migration messages_alerts force `seen_at` and `stale`, store a
 * `received_at` ahead of the database's clock as the clock's time, and write the first push's row of alert_outbox; the
 * API sets a disposition once, with who set it, and the trigger stamps when. Each closed list here is written from the
 * contracts' constant of the same name, and a database test holds the two to each other.
 */
export const contactMessages = pgTable(
  "contact_messages",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    /** `inbox` or `junk`: the folder the watcher read it in. */
    folder: text("folder").notNull(),
    /** The folder's UIDVALIDITY and the message's UID: unique together with the folder. */
    uidvalidity: bigint("uidvalidity", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    uid: bigint("uid", { mode: "number" }).notNull(),
    /** The IMAP internal date, the time of final delivery at the mail host; never later than the database's clock. */
    receivedAt: ts("received_at").notNull(),
    /** Forced: clock_timestamp() at the insert. */
    seenAt: ts("seen_at").notNull(),
    /** Forced: received more than order_rules().stale_hours before it was seen, which raises no push. */
    stale: boolean("stale").notNull(),
    /** Null, or what the message turned out to be (CONTACT_DISPOSITIONS); once set it never changes. */
    disposition: text("disposition"),
    handledBy: uuid("handled_by").references(() => profiles.id, { onDelete: "restrict" }),
    /** Forced when the disposition is set. */
    handledAt: ts("handled_at"),
  },
  (t) => [
    unique("contact_messages_uid_key").on(t.folder, t.uidvalidity, t.uid),
    check("contact_messages_folder", sql`${t.folder} in ('inbox', 'junk')`),
    check("contact_messages_disposition", sql`${t.disposition} in ('order', 'referral', 'first_order_notice', 'preservation_request', 'scrutiny_decision', 'clarification', 'not_an_order')`),
    check("contact_messages_handled", sql`(${t.disposition} is null) = (${t.handledAt} is null)`),
    /** The Contact point screen, newest first by the time of receipt. */
    index("contact_messages_received_idx").on(t.receivedAt, t.id),
    /** The messages nobody handled: the home screen's count and the alert steps' subjects. */
    index("contact_messages_open_idx").on(t.receivedAt).where(sql`disposition is null`),
    fullAccess("contact_messages_api_all", apiRole),
    fullAccess("contact_messages_notify_all", notifyRole),
  ],
).enableRLS();

/**
 * One alert with its two legs: the watcher publishes its push (`pushed_at`), and the API mails it (`mailed_at`) when its
 * kind's mail is its sentence. Its facts are counts and times only. The subject of a time-driven alert (a message or an
 * order) has no foreign key, so a record's erasure never waits for an alert's row. Every row's created_at, pushed_at,
 * mailed_at and push_attempts are forced at insert for every role. The unique key of a time-driven alert's step,
 * alert_outbox_step_key (kind, message_id, order_id, step) NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE step IS NOT NULL, is made by hand in
 * the migration: drizzle cannot write NULLS NOT DISTINCT on a partial index.
 */
export const alertOutbox = pgTable(
  "alert_outbox",
  {
    id: bigint("id", { mode: "number" }).primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(),
    /** One of the contracts' ALERT_KIND_LIST. */
    kind: text("kind").notNull(),
    /** 3 or 5, ntfy's default and highest priority. */
    priority: smallint("priority").notNull(),
    /** The push topic: the phone on call, or every staff phone. */
    scope: text("scope").notNull(),
    /** Null for an alert an event raised; a running number from 0, counted for each kind and subject, for a time-driven one. */
    step: smallint("step"),
    facts: jsonb("facts").$type<Record<string, number | string>>().notNull(),
    messageId: uuid("message_id"),
    orderId: uuid("order_id"),
    /** Forced: clock_timestamp(). */
    createdAt: ts("created_at").notNull(),
    pushedAt: ts("pushed_at"),
    mailedAt: ts("mailed_at"),
    /** A count of failed publishes, for the log; no cap. */
    pushAttempts: integer("push_attempts").notNull(),
  },
  (t) => [
    check(
      "alert_outbox_kind",
      sql`${t.kind} in ('contact_mail', 'contact_mail_escalated', 'order_due', 'order_opened', 'order_corrected', 'order_effected', 'order_reinstated', 'order_unverified', 'hold_ending', 'report_owed', 'handover_undestroyed', 'copy_overdue', 'copy_taken', 'alert_channel_down', 'mailbox_unreachable', 'alert_test', 'moderation_urgent', 'moderation_waiting', 'moderation_burst', 'moderation_reads', 'moderation_reveal', 'moderation_csam_lifted', 'quarantine_due', 'quarantine_lost', 'release_undestroyed', 'seal_released', 'edge_purge_failed', 'head_unwitnessed', 'head_missed', 'automated_objection', 'automation_capped', 'automated_waiting', 'matcher_down', 'hold_ended_unreported', 'head_unmailed', 'import_image_flagged')`,
    ),
    check("alert_outbox_priority", sql`${t.priority} in (3, 5)`),
    check("alert_outbox_scope", sql`${t.scope} in ('on_call', 'all')`),
    check("alert_outbox_step", sql`${t.step} is null or ${t.step} >= 0`),
    // Counts and times only: an object of at most six members, each a number or a string of the form of an instant in UTC.
    // The paths are strict: in lax mode a member's list would be unwrapped and its numbers read as members.
    check(
      "alert_outbox_facts",
      sql`jsonb_typeof(${t.facts}) = 'object' and jsonb_array_length(jsonb_path_query_array(${t.facts}, 'strict $.*')) <= 6 and not jsonb_path_exists(${t.facts}, 'strict $.* ? (@.type() != "number" && !(@.type() == "string" && @ like_regex "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}([.][0-9]{1,6})?Z$"))')`,
    ),

    fullAccess("alert_outbox_notify_all", notifyRole),
  ],
